00045   193     """Mark one phase that was **not** executed.

00060   208     by the owner of the test.  It is never a broad ``Exception``, it
00061   209     never hides a real failure of the production and it is never used
00062   210     to swallow one.
00063   211     """
00064   212

00066   214 class _R07OrdinaryAssertion(AssertionError):

00072   220     really raised and really fails; the token is normalised so that the

00075   223     broad ``Exception``: an ordinary failure of the group that is not
00076   224     this one is never taken for it.

00093   241 
00094   242 class _OwnerRegistry:
00095   243     """The registry of the owners that the fixture of this module starts.
00096   244 
00097   245     The registry is **immediate**: an owner is registered at the moment
00098   246     of its construction or of its start and it is never discovered
00099   247     later from a product that may have dropped it.  A channel whose
00100   248     construction failed half way, a drain thread whose start took
00101   249     effect and a worker that the product retained are all in the
00102   250     registry, and the salvage of the fixture joins every one of them
00103   251     with an explicitly bounded wait.
00104   252 
00105   253     The registry owns **nothing**: it only remembers.  The product
00106   254     keeps its own owners and its own returned state, and the registry
00107   255     never claims that the product released a resource.
00108   256 
00109   257     CORRECTION 17 (M3): the registry also holds the **provenance** of
00110   258     every start that the observer of this module saw.  The provenance
00111   259     is the proof of the start of an owner: an owner whose start was
00112   260     never invoked is ``NEVER_STARTED``, an owner whose start did not
00113   261     return is ``UNKNOWN`` and an owner whose start returned is
00114   262     ``STARTED``.  The provenance is keyed by the **exact** thread
00115   263     object and it is never inferred from a name.
00116   264     """
00117   265 
00118   266     def __init__(self):
00119   267         self._lock = threading.Lock()
00120   268         self._entries = []
00121   269         self._sequence = 0
00122   270         self._threads = {}
00123   271 
00124   272     def register(self, name, owner, *, kind, seam):
00125   273         """Register one owner **immediately** and return its entry."""
00126   274         with self._lock:
00127   275             self._sequence += 1
00128   276             entry = {'name': name, 'owner': owner, 'kind': kind,
00129   277                      'seam': seam, 'order': self._sequence,
00130   278                      'registered_at': time.monotonic(),
00131   279                      'start_state': None, 'start_error': None}
00132   280             self._entries.append(entry)
00133   281             return entry
00134   282 
00135   283     def mark_starting(self, thread):
00136   284         """Register the **exact** thread object before its start.
00137   285 
00138   286         The registration happens **before** the original start is
00139   287         called: a thread whose start does not return is an owner of the
00140   288         round from that moment on and it is never forgotten.
00141   289         """
00142   290         with self._lock:
00143   291             self._sequence += 1
00144   292             entry = {'name': 'thread:%s#%d' % (thread.name, id(thread)),
00145   293                      'owner': thread, 'kind': 'thread',
00146   294                      'seam': 'thread.start', 'order': self._sequence,
00147   295                      'registered_at': time.monotonic(),
00148   296                      'start_state': 'STARTING', 'start_error': None}
00149   297             self._entries.append(entry)
00150   298             self._threads[id(thread)] = entry
00151   299             return entry
00152   300 
00153   301     def mark_started(self, thread):
00154   302         """The start of the thread returned: the owner really started."""
00155   303         with self._lock:
00156   304             entry = self._threads.get(id(thread))
00157   305             if entry is not None:
00158   306                 entry['start_state'] = 'STARTED'
00159   307             return entry
00160   308 
00161   309     def mark_failed(self, thread, error):
00162   310         """The start of the thread did not return: the owner is unknown."""
00163   311         with self._lock:
00164   312             entry = self._threads.get(id(thread))
00165   313             if entry is not None:
00166   314                 entry['start_state'] = 'FAILED'
00167   315                 entry['start_error'] = {'type': type(error).__name__,
00168   316                                         'detail': str(error)}
00169   317             return entry
00170   318 
00171   319     def pending_starts(self):
00172   320         """The starts that did not return yet."""
00173   321         with self._lock:
00174   322             return sum(1 for item in self._entries
00175   323                        if item['kind'] == 'thread'
00176   324                        and item['start_state'] == 'STARTING')
00177   325 
00178   326     def start_provenance(self):
00179   327         """The proven provenance of every start that the observer saw."""
00180   328         with self._lock:
00181   329             return {id(item['owner']): item['start_state']
00182   330                     for item in self._entries if item['kind'] == 'thread'}
00183   331 
00184   332     def generation(self):
00185   333         """The number of the owners that the registry holds.
00186   334 
00187   335         The generation is the **witness** of the quiescence of the
00188   336         round: a generation that did not change across a final
00189   337         resnapshot means that no new owner appeared after it.
00190   338         """
00191   339         with self._lock:
00192   340             return len(self._entries)
00193   341 
00194   342     def entries(self):
00195   343         """The entries of the registry in the order of their registration."""
00196   344         with self._lock:
00197   345             return list(self._entries)
00198   346 
00199   347     def facts(self):
00200   348         """The facts of the registry: an owner is named and never guessed."""
00201   349         return [{'name': item['name'], 'kind': item['kind'],
00202   350                  'seam': item['seam'], 'order': item['order'],
00203   351                  'start_state': item['start_state']}
00204   352                 for item in self.entries()]
00205   353 
00206   354 
00207   355 class _StartObserver:
00208   356     """The observer of the starts of the threads of one round.
00209   357 
00210   358     The observer is installed around the **original**
00211   359     ``threading.Thread.start``: it forwards every start and it never
00212   360     refuses one, it never blocks one and it never changes a decision of
00213   361     the production.  It only **observes** the start and it registers the
00214   362     **exact** thread object at the moment of the start, so that a
00215   363     thread that the product starts during the stop of the round is an
00216   364     owner of the round and it is never forgotten.
00217   365 
00218   366     The scope of the observer is the **actual** round that the fixture
00219   367     builds: the observer is armed before the round is started and it is
00220   368     disarmed only after the salvage of that round has finished.
00221   369     """
00222   370 
00223   371     def __init__(self, registry):
00224   372         self._registry = registry
00225   373         self._original = threading.Thread.start
00226   374         self.armed = False
00227   375         self.observed = []
00228   376 
00229   377     def install(self):
00230   378         """The context manager that installs the observer."""
00231   379         observer = self
00232   380 
00233   381         def observed_start(thread, *args, **kwargs):
00234   382             if not observer.armed:
00235   383                 return observer._original(thread, *args, **kwargs)
00236   384             observer._registry.mark_starting(thread)
00237   385             try:
00238   386                 result = observer._original(thread, *args, **kwargs)
00239   387             except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00240   388                 observer._registry.mark_failed(thread, error)
00241   389                 raise
00242   390             observer._registry.mark_started(thread)
00243   391             observer.observed.append({'id': id(thread), 'name': thread.name})
00244   392             return result
00245   393 
00246   394         return unittest.mock.patch.object(threading.Thread, 'start',
00247   395                                           observed_start)
00248   396 
00249   397     def arm(self):
00250   398         """The observation of the starts begins."""
00251   399         self.armed = True
00252   400 
00253   401     def disarm(self):
00254   402         """The observation of the starts ends."""
00255   403         self.armed = False

00257   405 
00258   406 class _PhaseLedger:
00259   407     """The ledger of the phases that the group of this module runs.
00260   408 
00261   409     The ledger remembers what was **entered** and what **ended**.  It
00262   410     never decides: a phase that was entered and that failed is a
00263   411     ``FAIL`` and only a phase that was never entered is a ``NOT_RUN``.
00264   412     The states are ``PLANNED``, ``ATTEMPTED``, ``PASSED``, ``FAIL`` and
00265   413     ``NOT_RUN`` and the two last states are terminal.
00266   414     """
00267   415 
00268   416     STATES = ('PLANNED', 'ATTEMPTED', 'PASSED', 'FAIL', 'NOT_RUN')
00269   417 
00270   418     def __init__(self):
00271   419         self._lock = threading.Lock()
00272   420         self._states = {}
00273   421         self._order = []
00274   422         self._reasons = {}
00275   423 
00276   424     def _plan_locked(self, name):
00277   425         if name not in self._states:
00278   426             self._states[name] = 'PLANNED'
00279   427             self._order.append(name)
00280   428 
00281   429     def plan(self, name):
00282   430         """Name one phase **before** it runs."""
00283   431         with self._lock:
00284   432             self._plan_locked(name)
00285   433             return name
00286   434 
00287   435     def attempt(self, name):
00288   436         """Mark that the operation of the phase was **entered**."""
00289   437         with self._lock:
00290   438             self._plan_locked(name)
00291   439             if self._states[name] == 'PLANNED':
00292   440                 self._states[name] = 'ATTEMPTED'
00293   441             return self._states[name]
00294   442 
00295   443     def finish(self, name, state, reason=None):
00296   444         """Close one phase; a closed phase is never reopened."""
00297   445         with self._lock:
00298   446             self._plan_locked(name)
00299   447             if self._states[name] in ('PASSED', 'FAIL', 'NOT_RUN'):
00300   448                 return self._states[name]
00301   449             self._states[name] = state
00302   450             if reason is not None:
00303   451                 self._reasons[name] = reason
00304   452             return state
00305   453 
00306   454     def pass_(self, name):
00307   455         """The phase held every one of its checks."""
00308   456         return self.finish(name, 'PASSED')
00309   457 
00310   458     def fail(self, name, reason=None):
00311   459         """The phase was executed and it failed."""
00312   460         return self.finish(name, 'FAIL', reason)
00313   461 
00314   462     def state(self, name):
00315   463         """The state of one phase."""
00316   464         with self._lock:
00317   465             return self._states.get(name, 'PLANNED')
00318   466 
00319   467     def names(self):
00320   468         """The names of the phases in the order of their planning."""
00321   469         with self._lock:
00322   470             return list(self._order)
00323   471 
00324   472     def reason(self, name):
00325   473         """The reason of the failure of one phase."""
00326   474         with self._lock:
00327   475             return self._reasons.get(name)
00328   476 
00329   477 
00330   478 class _RegistryCustody:
00331   479     """The custody seam of the fixture: it registers what it retains.
00332   480 
00333   481     The custody of the launcher is a **supported** seam of the
00334   482     production: a channel registers itself with it **before** it builds
00335   483     anything.  The seam of the fixture forwards every call to the
00336   484     original custody of the round and it registers the retained owner
00337   485     in the registry of the fixture at the moment of the retention.
00338   486 
00339   487     A channel whose construction failed after its drain thread was
00340   488     started is therefore in the registry of the fixture even when the
00341   489     constructor never returned the channel to the fixture.
00342   490     """
00343   491 
00344   492     def __init__(self, registry, name, original=None):
00345   493         self._registry = registry
00346   494         self._name = name
00347   495         self._original = original
00348   496 
00349   497     def retain(self, kind, resource, detail=None, launch=None):
00350   498         self._registry.register('%s:%s' % (self._name, kind), resource,
00351   499                                 kind=kind, seam='custody.retain')
00352   500         if self._original is None:
00353   501             return resource
00354   502         # The **original** signature of the custody is honoured: the
00355   503         # aggregate of a launch takes three arguments and the table of
00356   504         # the launcher takes four.
00357   505         return self._original.retain(kind, resource, detail)
00358   506 
00359   507     def forget(self, resource):
00360   508         if self._original is None:
00361   509             return None
00362   510         return self._original.forget(resource)
00363   511 
00364   512 
00365   513 def _owner_start_state(thread, hint=None):
00366   514     """The start state of one owner of the round.
00367   515 
00368   516     The state is one of ``'STARTED'``, ``'NEVER_STARTED'`` or
00369   517     ``'UNKNOWN'``.  ``UNKNOWN`` is the state of an owner whose start
00370   518     did not return and of an owner whose liveness could not be asked:
00371   519     such an owner may still come up, it is never taken for an owner
00372   520     that never started and it **fails the proof** of the cleanup.
00373   521 
00374   522     CORRECTION 17 (M3): ``NEVER_STARTED`` is returned **only** when the
00375   523     provenance of the start **proves** it: the owner does not exist at
00376   524     all, or the registry of the fixture observed that its start was
00377   525     never invoked.  An owner without an identity and without a
00378   526     provenance is ``UNKNOWN``: it is never guessed to be an owner that
00379   527     never started.
00380   528     """
00381   529     if thread is None:
00382   530         return 'NEVER_STARTED'
00383   531     # CORRECTION 18 (M3): the query of the identity of the owner is
00384   532     # **not** swallowed here any more.  A failure of it is a fact of the
00385   533     # cleanup and the guard of the caller records it with its exact type
00386   534     # and its exact detail: a silent ``UNKNOWN`` without a diagnostic
00387   535     # would hide the failure of the classification and it would let an
00388   536     # unknown identity pass for a proved exit.
00389   537     ident = getattr(thread, 'ident', None)
00390   538     if ident is not None:
00391   539         return 'STARTED'
00392   540     if hint in ('STARTED', 'NEVER_STARTED', 'UNKNOWN'):
00393   541         return hint
00394   542     return 'UNKNOWN'
00395   543 
00396   544 
00397   545 def _salvage_threads(owners, *, seconds=10.0, states=None, total_seconds=30.0,
00398   546                      interrupts=None):
00399   547     """Join the owners that really started and report their liveness.
00400   548 
00401   549     The salvage is the work of the **test** and it is **separate** from
00402   550     the returned state of the product: it never renews a deadline of
00403   551     the round, it never erases a retained resource of the product and
00404   552     it never claims that the product released it.
00405   553 
00406   554     Every owner that really started is joined with an explicitly
00407   555     bounded wait and its liveness is reported.  An owner that never
00408   556     started is reported and **never** joined.  An owner whose start
00409   557     state is ``UNKNOWN`` is reported as unknown: it is never joined as
00410   558     if it had ended and it fails the proof of the cleanup.
00411   559 
00412   560     CORRECTION 17 (M3): **every** owner is attempted.  A failure of the
00413   561     classification of an owner, of its join or of its liveness query
00414   562     never aborts the iteration: the error is **retained** in a list
00415   563     with its kind, its exact type and its detail, and it fails the
00416   564     proof of the cleanup.  The wait of an owner is cropped by the
00417   565     remaining budget of the salvage, so that the salvage is bounded as
00418   566     a whole.
00419   567 
00420   568     CORRECTION 18 (M3): the **exact** object of a ``KeyboardInterrupt``
00421   569     or of a ``SystemExit`` is retained in the ``interrupts`` list of the
00422   570     caller: the identity of the cancellation survives every best effort
00423   571     cleanup and it is re-raised by the owner of the cleanup when no
00424   572     other failure is unwinding.  The error that is written in the
00425   573     document keeps its exact type and its exact detail; the **object**
00426   574     itself never enters a document.
00427   575     """
00428   576     facts = []
00429   577     hints = states or {}
00430   578     deadline = time.monotonic() + max(0.0, total_seconds)
00431   579     for name, thread in owners:
00432   580         state = None
00433   581         errors = []
00434   582         try:
00435   583             state = _owner_start_state(thread, hints.get(name))
00436   584         except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00437   585             errors.append({'kind': 'STATE', 'type': type(error).__name__,
00438   586                            'detail': str(error)})
00439   587             _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00440   588             state = 'UNKNOWN'
00441   589         if state != 'STARTED':
00442   590             facts.append({'name': name, 'start_state': state,
00443   591                           'started': None if state == 'UNKNOWN' else False,
00444   592                           'alive': None, 'joined': None, 'errors': errors})
00445   593             continue
00446   594         try:
00447   595             wait = max(0.0, min(seconds, deadline - time.monotonic()))
00448   596             thread.join(wait)
00449   597         except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00450   598             errors.append({'kind': 'JOIN', 'type': type(error).__name__,
00451   599                            'detail': str(error)})
00452   600             _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00453   601         alive = None
00454   602         try:
00455   603             alive = bool(thread.is_alive())
00456   604         except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00457   605             errors.append({'kind': 'LIVENESS', 'type': type(error).__name__,
00458   606                            'detail': str(error)})
00459   607             _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00460   608         facts.append({'name': name, 'start_state': state, 'started': True,
00461   609                       'alive': alive, 'joined': (alive is False),
00462   610                       'errors': errors})
00463   611     return facts
00464   612 
00465   613 
00466   614 def _note_interruption(interrupts, error):
00467   615     """Retain the **exact** object of an interruption of the cleanup.
00468   616 
00469   617     A ``KeyboardInterrupt`` and a ``SystemExit`` are the identity of the
00470   618     cancellation of the round: they are retained as the objects
00471   619     themselves and they are re-raised by the owner of the cleanup when
00472   620     no other failure is unwinding.
00473   621     """
00474   622     if interrupts is None:
00475   623         return False
00476   624     if isinstance(error, (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit)):
00477   625         interrupts.append(error)
00478   626         return True
00479   627     return False
00480   628 
00481   629 
00482   630 def _interruption_facts(interrupts):
00483   631     """The **durable** diagnostics of the exact interruptions.
00484   632 
00485   633     CORRECTION 19 (M3): the exact object of a cancellation never enters a
00486   634     document - only its exact type and its exact detail do.  The
00487   635     diagnostics of the cancellations of a cleanup are **kept** in the
00488   636     document of the cleanup: they are never reduced to a type and a
00489   637     detail of the last error and they are never discarded next to an
00490   638     original failure.
00491   639     """
00492   640     return [{'type': type(item).__name__, 'detail': repr(item)}
00493   641             for item in (interrupts or [])]
00494   642 
00495   643 
00496   644 def _assert_salvage_proved(facts, message):
00497   645     """The proof that the fixture released every owner that it started.
00498   646 
00499   647     An owner with an **unknown** start state fails the proof: it is
00500   648     never taken for an owner that never started and it is never taken
00501   649     for an owner that ended.  An owner that met an error fails the
00502   650     proof as well: a cleanup that met an error is never a success.
00503   651     """
00504   652     for item in facts:
00505   653         assert item['start_state'] != 'UNKNOWN', \
00506   654             '%s: the owner %s has an unknown start state' \
00507   655             % (message, item['name'])
00508   656         errors = item.get('errors') or []
00509   657         assert not errors, \
00510   658             '%s: the owner %s met %s' % (message, item['name'], errors)
00511   659         if item['started']:
00512   660             assert item['alive'] is False, \
00513   661                 '%s: the owner %s was left behind' % (message, item['name'])
00514   662 
00515   663 
00516   664 def _prove_salvage(facts, message):
00517   665     """The proof of the cleanup of a round, as a **fact**.
00518   666 
00519   667     The proof is **run** in every case - also while an ordinary failure
00520   668     is already unwinding - and it returns the failure of the proof
00521   669     instead of raising it: a failure of the proof never replaces the
00522   670     failure that is already unwinding and it is never discarded.
00523   671     """
00524   672     for item in facts:
00525   673         errors = item.get('errors') or []
00526   674         if item['start_state'] == 'UNKNOWN':
00527   675             return '%s: the owner %s has an unknown start state%s' \
00528   676                 % (message, item['name'], _errors_suffix(errors))
00529   677         if errors:
00530   678             return '%s: the owner %s met %s' \
00531   679                 % (message, item['name'], errors)
00532   680         if item['started'] and item['alive'] is not False:
00533   681             return '%s: the owner %s was left behind' % (message, item['name'])
00534   682     return None
00535   683 
00536   684 
00537   685 def _errors_suffix(errors):
00538   686     """The diagnostic of the errors of one owner of the round."""
00539   687     if not errors:
00540   688         return ''
00541   689     return ' (%s)' % (errors,)
00542   690 
00543   691 
00544   692 def _capture_stop(session, original_broker=None, *, interrupts=None):
00545   693     """The **returned** state of the public stop of a round.
00546   694 
00547   695     The result of the stop is captured **before** the salvage of the
00548   696     fixture: the salvage is the work of the test and it never replaces
00549   697     the returned state of the product.  An exception of the stop is
00550   698     captured and it is never discarded.
00551   699 
00552   700     CORRECTION 17 (M3): the live state and the retention of the round
00553   701     are read **now**, in the moment of the failure, and the **actual**
00554   702     facts of the evidence of the session are kept with their **real**
00555   703     keys.  The identities of the retained resource are the live objects
00556   704     of the session: the retained broker is compared with the broker of
00557   705     the round that was captured **before** the stop, and a broker that
00558   706     is gone is ``None`` and never the identity of ``None``.
00559   707 
00560   708     CORRECTION 18 (M3): a stop that raised and a snapshot of the
00561   709     evidence that failed are **facts of the cleanup** and they never
00562   710     certify it: the helper ``_stop_proof_failure`` turns them into the
00563   711     failure of the proof.  The **exact** object of an interruption is
00564   712     retained in the ``interrupts`` list of the caller.
00565   713     """
00566   714     captured = {'returned': None, 'exception': None, 'live_state': None,
00567   715                 'evidence': None, 'evidence_state': None,
00568   716                 'evidence_broker_retained': None,
00569   717                 'evidence_failures': None,
00570   718                 'evidence_background_threads': None,
00571   719                 'evidence_closer_start_state': None,
00572   720                 'retained_broker_is_original': None,
00573   721                 'retained_broker_id': None, 'snapshot_error': None}
00574   722     if session is None:
00575   723         return captured
00576   724     try:
00577   725         captured['returned'] = session.stop()
00578   726     except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the failure stays visible
00579   727         captured['exception'] = {'type': type(error).__name__,
00580   728                                  'detail': str(error)}
00581   729         _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00582   730     try:
00583   731         captured['live_state'] = session.state
00584   732         broker = getattr(session, 'broker', None)
00585   733         captured['retained_broker_id'] = None if broker is None else id(broker)
00586   734         if original_broker is not None:
00587   735             captured['retained_broker_is_original'] = \
00588   736                 (broker is original_broker)
00589   737         evidence = session.evidence()
00590   738         captured['evidence'] = evidence
00591   739         captured['evidence_state'] = evidence['state']
00592   740         captured['evidence_broker_retained'] = evidence['broker_retained']
00593   741         captured['evidence_failures'] = list(evidence['failures'])
00594   742         captured['evidence_background_threads'] = list(
00595   743             evidence['background_threads'])
00596   744         captured['evidence_closer_start_state'] = evidence['closer_start_state']
00597   745     except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the failure stays visible
00598   746         captured['snapshot_error'] = {'type': type(error).__name__,
00599   747                                       'detail': str(error)}
00600   748         _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00601   749     return captured
00602   750 
00603   751 
00604   752 def _stop_proof_failure(captured, message):
00605   753     """The failure of the cleanup that the capture of the stop carries.
00606   754 
00607   755     A stop that raised and a snapshot of the evidence that failed are
00608   756     **facts** of the cleanup: they are never ignored and they never
00609   757     certify that the round was cleaned.  The helper returns ``None``
00610   758     when the capture carries no error at all.
00611   759     """
00612   760     problems = []
00613   761     if captured.get('exception') is not None:
00614   762         problems.append('the stop of the round met %s'
00615   763                         % (captured['exception'],))
00616   764     if captured.get('snapshot_error') is not None:
00617   765         problems.append('the snapshot of the evidence of the round met %s'
00618   766                         % (captured['snapshot_error'],))
00619   767     if not problems:
00620   768         return None
00621   769     return '%s: %s' % (message, '; '.join(problems))
00622   770 
00623   771 
00624   772 def _join_details(*parts):
00625   773     """The detail of a failure: every part that carries a fact.
00626   774 
00627   775     CORRECTION 18 (M2): the original failure of the phase and every
00628   776     diagnostic of its cleanup are **joined**: neither of them replaces
00629   777     the other and none of them is dropped.
00630   778     """
00631   779     return '; '.join([part for part in parts if part])
00632   780 
00633   781 
00634   782 def _cleanup_detail(cleanup_errors, write_errors):
00635   783     """The diagnostic of the cleanup errors of one phase.
00636   784 
00637   785     CORRECTION 18 (M2): the errors of the cleanup are a **list** and
00638   786     they are never overwritten: the detail names **every** one of them
00639   787     and it names the errors of the writing of the evidence as well.
00640   788     """
00641   789     parts = []
00642   790     for item in cleanup_errors:
00643   791         parts.append('%s: %s' % (item.get('kind'), item.get('detail')))
00644   792     for item in write_errors:
00645   793         parts.append('the writing of the evidence of %s failed: %s'
00646   794                      % (item.get('name'), item.get('detail')))
00647   795     if not parts:
00648   796         return None
00649   797     return '; '.join(parts)

00651   799 
00652   800 def _session_owners(session, prefix='session', hints=None):
00653   801     """The owners that the session of the round really started.
00654   802 
00655   803     The registry is read from the session itself: the background
00656   804     threads of the round and the closer threads that it really built.
00657   805     A closer that never started is reported as such and it is never
00658   806     joined.  A thread whose start did not return is **UNKNOWN**: it
00659   807     keeps its owner in the session and it may still come up.
00660   808     """
00661   809     owners = []
00662   810     if session is None:
00663   811         return owners
00664   812     records = getattr(session, '_background_threads', None) or {}
00665   813     for kind in sorted(records):
00666   814         record = records[kind] or {}
00667   815         name = '%s:background-%s' % (prefix, str(kind))
00668   816         owners.append((name, record.get('thread')))
00669   817         if hints is None:
00670   818             continue
00671   819         state = record.get('state')
00672   820         if state == 'STARTING':
00673   821             hints[name] = 'UNKNOWN'
00674   822         elif state == 'FAILED' and not record.get('started'):
00675   823             hints[name] = 'NEVER_STARTED'
00676   824     closer_state = getattr(session, '_closer_start_state', None)
00677   825     for index, thread in enumerate(getattr(session, '_closer_threads', None)
00678   826                                    or []):
00679   827         name = '%s:closer-%d' % (prefix, index)
00680   828         owners.append((name, thread))
00681   829         if hints is not None and closer_state == 'STARTING':
00682   830             hints[name] = 'UNKNOWN'
00683   831     return owners
00684   832 
00685   833 
00686   834 def _endpoint_owners(prefix, endpoint, hints=None):
00687   835     """The owners that one endpoint of the round really started.
00688   836 
00689   837     The read worker and the write worker of the endpoint are the
00690   838     owners that the endpoint really started.  A worker that the
00691   839     endpoint **retained** is a worker whose start did not return: its
00692   840     state is **UNKNOWN** and it fails the proof of the cleanup.
00693   841     """
00694   842     owners = []
00695   843     if endpoint is None:
00696   844         return owners
00697   845     for role, label in (('_reader', 'read'), ('_writer', 'write')):
00698   846         worker = getattr(endpoint, role, None)
00699   847         if worker is None:
00700   848             continue
00701   849         owners.append(('%s:%s-worker' % (prefix, label), worker))
00702   850     for index, worker in enumerate(getattr(endpoint, '_retained', None)
00703   851                                    or []):
00704   852         name = '%s:retained-%d' % (prefix, index)
00705   853         owners.append((name, worker))
00706   854         if hints is not None:
00707   855             hints[name] = 'UNKNOWN'
00708   856     return owners
00709   857 
00710   858 
00711   859 def _channel_owners(channel, prefix, hints=None):
00712   860     """The owners that the channel of the round really started.
00713   861 
00714   862     The drain thread of the channel and the workers of its two
00715   863     endpoints are the owners of the round that really started.  A worker
00716   864     that was never started is reported as such and it is never joined.
00717   865     """
00718   866     owners = []
00719   867     if channel is None:
00720   868         return owners
00721   869     owners.append((prefix + ':drain', getattr(channel, '_thread', None)))
00722   870     if hints is not None:
00723   871         # The drain thread of a channel is started **inside** the
00724   872         # constructor of the channel: a channel whose construction
00725   873         # failed at the start of its drain owns a drain thread whose
00726   874         # start did not return and it may still come up.
00727   875         hints[prefix + ':drain'] = 'UNKNOWN'
00728   876     reader = getattr(channel, '_reader', None)
00729   877     writer = getattr(channel, '_writer', None)
00730   878     for endpoint, label in ((reader, 'read'), (writer, 'write')):
00731   879         owners.extend(_endpoint_owners('%s:%s' % (prefix, label), endpoint,
00732   880                                        hints))
00733   881     return owners
00734   882 
00735   883 
00736   884 def _registry_owners(registry, session=None, channel=None, prefix='round',
00737   885                       errors=None, interrupts=None):
00738   886     """Every owner of the round: the registered ones and the live ones.
00739   887 
00740   888     The registry of the fixture holds the owners that were registered
00741   889     **immediately** - a channel that was constructed, an endpoint that
00742   890     was built, a session that was created.  The session and the
00743   891     channel that are still reachable are added to them, so that a
00744   892     thread that the product started after the registration is never
00745   893     forgotten.  One owner is never in the list twice: the identity of
00746   894     the thread decides and not its name.
00747   895 
00748   896     CORRECTION 19 (M3): the traversal is **best effort**.  The query
00749   897     of one container never aborts the traversal and it never replaces
00750   898     the owners of the round with an empty list: every other owner is
00751   899     still attempted.  The **exact** thread objects that the start
00752   900     registry observed are retained **first** and they are an
00753   901     independent fallback - a failure of the query of a container never
00754   902     loses them.  Every failure is retained with its exact type and its
00755   903     exact detail and the **exact** object of an interruption is kept.
00756   904     """
00757   905     owners = []
00758   906     hints = {}
00759   907     seen = set()
00760   908     kinds = set()
00761   909 
00762   910     def add(items):
00763   911         for name, thread in items:
00764   912             key = ('thread', id(thread)) if thread is not None \
00765   913                 else ('name', name)
00766   914             if key in seen:
00767   915                 continue
00768   916             seen.add(key)
00769   917             owners.append((name, thread))
00770   918 
00771   919     def note(kind, error):
00772   920         """Retain one failure of the traversal, never swallow it."""
00773   921         if errors is not None:
00774   922             errors.append({'kind': kind, 'type': type(error).__name__,
00775   923                            'detail': str(error)})
00776   924         _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00777   925 
00778   926     try:
00779   927         entries = registry.entries()
00780   928     except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00781   929         note('REGISTRY_ENTRIES', error)
00782   930         entries = []
00783   931     # CORRECTION 19 (M3): the **exact** thread objects that the start
00784   932     # registry observed are retained **first** and they are an
00785   933     # independent fallback: a failure of the query of a container never
00786   934     # loses them and it never replaces the owners of the round with an
00787   935     # empty list.  They are merged into the owners **after** the
00788   936     # traversal, so that the name of an owner that a container really
00789   937     # knows is never replaced by the name of the registry.
00790   938     observed = [(item.get('name'), item.get('owner'))
00791   939                 for item in entries
00792   940                 if item.get('kind') == 'thread'
00793   941                 and item.get('owner') is not None]
00794   942     for entry in entries:
00795   943         name = entry.get('name')
00796   944         owner = entry.get('owner')
00797   945         kind = entry.get('kind')
00798   946         if kind == 'thread':
00799   947             add([(name, owner)])
00800   948             continue
00801   949         try:
00802   950             if kind == 'channel':
00803   951                 items = _channel_owners(owner, name, hints)
00804   952             elif kind == 'endpoint':
00805   953                 items = _endpoint_owners(name, owner, hints)
00806   954             elif kind == 'session':
00807   955                 items = _session_owners(owner, name, hints)
00808   956             else:
00809   957                 items = [(name, owner)]
00810   958         except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00811   959             # the traversal continues: the owners that follow this one
00812   960             # are still attempted and the exact thread object of this
00813   961             # entry is still an owner of the round.
00814   962             note('OWNER_QUERY', error)
00815   963             if isinstance(owner, threading.Thread):
00816   964                 add([(name, owner)])
00817   965             continue
00818   966         kinds.add(kind)
00819   967         add(items)
00820   968     try:
00821   969         if session is not None and 'session' not in kinds:
00822   970             add(_session_owners(session, '%s:session' % prefix, hints))
00823   971     except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00824   972         note('SESSION_QUERY', error)
00825   973     try:
00826   974         if channel is not None and 'channel' not in kinds:
00827   975             add(_channel_owners(channel, '%s:channel' % prefix, hints))
00828   976     except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00829   977         note('CHANNEL_QUERY', error)
00830   978     # CORRECTION 19 (M3): the fallback of the observed threads: every
00831   979     # exact thread object that the start registry saw is an owner of the
00832   980     # round.  The merge is **idempotent**: an owner that the traversal
00833   981     # already named keeps its name and its hint.
00834   982     for name, thread in observed:
00835   983         add([(name, thread)])
00836   984     # CORRECTION 17 (M3): the provenance of the starts that the
00837   985     # observer of the fixture saw is the **proven** provenance of the
00838   986     # start of an owner.  It is keyed by the exact thread object and it
00839   987     # never replaces the hint of the production: a thread whose start
00840   988     # returned is ``STARTED`` and a thread whose start did not return is
00841   989     # ``UNKNOWN``.
00842   990     try:
00843   991         provenance = registry.start_provenance() if registry is not None else {}
00844   992     except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00845   993         note('PROVENANCE', error)
00846   994         provenance = {}
00847   995     for name, thread in owners:
00848   996         if thread is None:
00849   997             continue
00850   998         state = provenance.get(id(thread))
00851   999         if state == 'STARTED':
00852  1000             hints[name] = 'STARTED'
00853  1001         elif state in ('STARTING', 'FAILED'):
00854  1002             hints[name] = 'UNKNOWN'
00855  1003     return owners, hints
00856  1004 
00857  1005 
00858  1006 def _drain_owners(registry, session=None, channel=None, prefix='round', *,
00859  1007                   seconds=10.0, budget=30.0, release=None, interrupts=None):
00860  1008     """The bounded drain of the owners of one round.
00861  1009 
00862  1010     CORRECTION 17 (M3): the drain repeats, **boundedly**, until the
00863  1011     owners of the round are quiescent and really joined.  The bound of
00864  1012     the drain is **one** overall bound: the wait of an owner is cropped
00865  1013     by the remaining budget and the budget is never reset - neither
00866  1014     between the rounds of the drain nor between the rounds of the test.
00867  1015 
00868  1016     The quiescence of the round is asserted **after** the drain and
00869  1017     never before it: a round that is not quiescent is a failure of the
00870  1018     cleanup, the gates of the round are still released and **all** the
00871  1019     registered owners are still attempted.
00872  1020 
00873  1021     CORRECTION 18 (M3): the enumeration of the owners and the reading
00874  1022     of the generation of the registry are **one** observation.  The
00875  1023     generation is read **before** the exact owners are enumerated and
00876  1024     it is read **again** right after the enumeration and once more
00877  1025     after the joined producer threads of the iteration.  All of these
00878  1026     readings must agree and the **final** exact-owner resnapshot must
00879  1027     contain every owner of the enumeration: a thread that was started
00880  1028     between the enumeration and the reading of the generation is never
00881  1029     certified as quiescent and it is never left behind.
00882  1030 
00883  1031     Every error of the drain - the enumeration, the release of the
00884  1032     gates, the classification of an owner, its join and its liveness
00885  1033     query - is **retained** in a list with its exact type and its exact
00886  1034     detail and it fails the proof of the cleanup.  **Every** iteration
00887  1035     is kept: an error of an earlier iteration is never erased by a
00888  1036     later iteration that really ended the threads.  A failure never
00889  1037     aborts the iteration and it never skips the final result of the
00890  1038     round.  The drain never renews a deadline of the product.
00891  1039 
00892  1040     CORRECTION 19 (M3): every read of the drain - the generation, the
00893  1041     pending starts and the final resnapshot - is **best effort** and it
00894  1042     never skips the owners that follow it.  The release of the gates is
00895  1043     **one action per gate**: a failure of one gate never skips the gate
00896  1044     that follows it.  The traversal of the owners never replaces the
00897  1045     owners of the round with an empty list and the exact thread objects
00898  1046     that the start registry observed are always retained.
00899  1047     """
00900  1048     deadline = time.monotonic() + max(0.0, budget)
00901  1049     attempts = []
00902  1050     errors = []
00903  1051     owners = []
00904  1052     hints = {}
00905  1053     salvage = []
00906  1054     all_salvage = []
00907  1055     quiescent = False
00908  1056 
00909  1057     def read_generation(label):
00910  1058         """Read the generation of the registry, guarded.
00911  1059 
00912  1060         CORRECTION 19 (M3): the reading of the generation is **best
00913  1061         effort**: a failure of it is a fact of the cleanup and it never
00914  1062         skips the owners that follow it.
00915  1063         """
00916  1064         try:
00917  1065             return registry.generation()
00918  1066         except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00919  1067             errors.append({'kind': label, 'type': type(error).__name__,
00920  1068                            'detail': str(error)})
00921  1069             _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00922  1070             return None
00923  1071 
00924  1072     def read_pending(label):
00925  1073         """Read the pending starts of the registry, guarded."""
00926  1074         try:
00927  1075             return registry.pending_starts()
00928  1076         except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00929  1077             errors.append({'kind': label, 'type': type(error).__name__,
00930  1078                            'detail': str(error)})
00931  1079             _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00932  1080             return None
00933  1081 
00934  1082     while True:
00935  1083         # the generation of the registry is read **before** the exact
00936  1084         # owners are enumerated
00937  1085         generation_before = read_generation('GENERATION_BEFORE')
00938  1086         try:
00939  1087             owners, hints = _registry_owners(registry, session=session,
00940  1088                                               channel=channel, prefix=prefix,
00941  1089                                               errors=errors,
00942  1090                                               interrupts=interrupts)
00943  1091         except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00944  1092             errors.append({'kind': 'ENUMERATION',
00945  1093                            'type': type(error).__name__,
00946  1094                            'detail': str(error)})
00947  1095             _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00948  1096             # CORRECTION 19 (M3): the owners of the previous observation
00949  1097             # are **retained**: a failure of the enumeration never loses
00950  1098             # them and it never replaces them with an empty list.
00951  1099         # ... and it is read **again** right after the enumeration: a
00952  1100         # start that happened between the two readings is a change of
00953  1101         # the generation and the enumeration is repeated.
00954  1102         generation_after = read_generation('GENERATION_AFTER')
00955  1103         snapshot = {'generation_before': generation_before,
00956  1104                     'generation_after': generation_after,
00957  1105                     'generation': generation_after,
00958  1106                     'pending': read_pending('PENDING'),
00959  1107                     'owners': [name for name, _ in owners],
00960  1108                     'errors': list(errors)}
00961  1109         attempts.append(snapshot)
00962  1110         if release is not None:
00963  1111             # CORRECTION 19 (M3): the release of the gates is **best
00964  1112             # effort**: every gate is released on its own and a failure
00965  1113             # of one gate never skips the gate that follows it.
00966  1114             actions = (release if isinstance(release, (list, tuple))
00967  1115                        else [release])
00968  1116             for action in actions:
00969  1117                 try:
00970  1118                     action()
00971  1119                 except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001
00972  1120                     errors.append({'kind': 'RELEASE',
00973  1121                                    'type': type(error).__name__,
00974  1122                                    'detail': str(error)})
00975  1123                     _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00976  1124         remaining = max(0.0, deadline - time.monotonic())
00977  1125         salvage = _salvage_threads(owners, states=hints, seconds=seconds,
00978  1126                                    total_seconds=remaining,
00979  1127                                    interrupts=interrupts)
00980  1128         # CORRECTION 18 (M3): **every** iteration of the drain is kept -
00981  1129         # the failure of an earlier iteration is never erased by a later
00982  1130         # iteration that ended the threads.
00983  1131         all_salvage.extend(salvage)
00984  1132         # The **final** exact-owner resnapshot: it is taken after the
00985  1133         # joined producer threads of this iteration and it must agree
00986  1134         # with the enumeration of this iteration.
00987  1135         final_generation = read_generation('FINAL_GENERATION')
00988  1136         try:
00989  1137             final_owners, _final_hints = _registry_owners(
00990  1138                 registry, session=session, channel=channel, prefix=prefix,
00991  1139                 errors=errors, interrupts=interrupts)
00992  1140         except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00993  1141             errors.append({'kind': 'FINAL_ENUMERATION',
00994  1142                            'type': type(error).__name__,
00995  1143                            'detail': str(error)})
00996  1144             _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00997  1145             final_owners = []
00998  1146         # and the generation is read **again** after the final
00999  1147         # resnapshot: a start that happened during it is a change of the
01000  1148         # generation and the drain repeats.
01001  1149         final_generation_after = read_generation('FINAL_GENERATION_AFTER')
01002  1150         final_names = [name for name, _ in final_owners]
01003  1151         missing = [name for name in snapshot['owners']
01004  1152                    if name not in final_names]
01005  1153         late = [name for name in final_names
01006  1154                 if name not in snapshot['owners']]
01007  1155         pending = read_pending('FINAL_PENDING')
01008  1156         stable = (generation_before == generation_after
01009  1157                   and final_generation == generation_after
01010  1158                   and final_generation_after == generation_after
01011  1159                   and not missing and not late)
01012  1160         quiescent = (pending == 0 and stable
01013  1161                      and _prove_salvage(salvage, prefix) is None)
01014  1162         if quiescent or time.monotonic() >= deadline:
01015  1163             break
01016  1164         # the drain is **bounded** and it never spins: the next attempt
01017  1165         # follows a short pause and it happens inside the same budget
01018  1166         time.sleep(0.01)
01019  1167     proof = _prove_salvage(all_salvage, prefix)
01020  1168     if proof is None and errors:
01021  1169         proof = '%s: the drain met %s' % (prefix, errors)
01022  1170     # CORRECTION 19 (M2/M3): a round that is **not** quiescent is a
01023  1171     # failure of the cleanup even when every owner that the salvage saw
01024  1172     # was really joined: the final resnapshot of the drain found an
01025  1173     # owner that no join released, and the proof of the cleanup says so.
01026  1174     if proof is None and not quiescent:
01027  1175         proof = ('%s: the owners of the round were not quiescent' % prefix)
01028  1176     return {'owners': owners, 'hints': hints, 'salvage': salvage,
01029  1177             'all_salvage': all_salvage,
01030  1178             'attempts': attempts, 'proof': proof, 'errors': errors,
01031  1179             'quiescent': bool(quiescent)}
01032  1180

01035  1183 # -- N10-R01: the control handle of a process ------------------------------
01036  1184 
01037  1185 def test_n10_r01_the_control_handle_is_closed_only_after_the_exit(tmp_path):

00347  5445 def _m09_timeout_phase(document, plan, tmp_path, *, phase, confirm_the_worker,
00348  5446                         hold_the_worker, barrier_probe='EXACT',
00349  5447                         expect_barrier='PASSED', inventory=None, ledger=None):
00350  5448     """The dynamic schedule of the M09 obligation of this group.
00351  5449 
00352  5450     The schedule is the **production** one: a real ordinary fault is
00353  5451     published for the current generation of the read of the real chain,
00354  5452     the effective timeout of the round arrives **before** the endpoint
00355  5453     consumes the outcome, and the coordination of the round - a
00356  5454     confirmed one or a failed one - preserves the exact original error
00357  5455     object and its code.  The timeout and the failure of the
00358  5456     coordination are **parallel** facts: they never replace the failure
00359  5457     that was really published.
00360  5458 
00361  5459     Every fact of the phase is the fact that the production returned.
00362  5460 
00363  5461     RECONCILIATION (N1 correction 14, F5): the schedule of the **failed**
00364  5462     coordination reached the selection point of the production without a
00365  5463     published fault: the cancel primitive of the round enqueued the
00366  5464     fault of the read and returned immediately, so the coordination
00367  5465     could finish before the worker had published the immutable outcome
00368  5466     of its generation.  The parallel fact of the timeout could then not
00369  5467     be read at all.  The seam of the failed coordination now publishes
00370  5468     the real primitive fault and waits, bounded, for the **immutable
00371  5469     outcome of that specific generation** before the cancel primitive
00372  5470     returns, while the worker of the round is held inside its own
00373  5471     final close and release tail: the real bounded join of the
00374  5472     coordination still FAILS and the coordination error stays a
00375  5473     **parallel** fact of the original error of the round.  The
00376  5474     confirmed coordination and the required order of the schedule
00377  5475     (fault published before the timeout, consumed after it) stay
00378  5476     separate and unchanged.
00379  5477 
00380  5478     N1 correction 15 (M2): the wait of the seam for the outcome of the
00381  5479     generation is a **checked** barrier and it **fails closed**.  The
00382  5480     barrier demands the immutable outcome of the **exact** generation,
00383  5481     the expected kind of the ordinary failure and the **exact** original
00384  5482     error object **before** the cancel primitive returns, and it stores
00385  5483     the checked order of the three facts.  A missing outcome, an outcome
00386  5484     of another generation, another kind of failure and another error
00387  5485     object are an **explicit refusal** of the premise of the test: the
00388  5486     primitive never returns ``REQUESTED`` as if the barrier had passed.
00389  5487     The production catches the ordinary exceptions of the seam, so the
00390  5488     outer test reads the premise from the record of the barrier itself
00391  5489     and it captures that record **before** the main assertions of the
00392  5490     phase.
00393  5491 
00394  5492     The two negative subcases of the barrier (``ABSENT`` and
00395  5493     ``WRONG_GENERATION``) drive the **same** failed coordination with a
00396  5494     bounded transparent seam that forces an absent outcome and an
00397  5495     outcome of another generation.  Their premise is **refused** and
00398  5496     they are never counted as a successful failed coordination.
00399  5497 
00400  5498     The **confirmed** coordination does not use the barrier at all: it
00401  5499     waits for the real exit of the worker and the record of the barrier
00402  5500     says that it never ran.  The expectation of the phase names the
00403  5501     three cases: ``PASSED`` for the failed coordination, ``REFUSED`` for
00404  5502     the two negative subcases and ``NOT_APPLICABLE`` for the confirmed
00405  5503     coordination.
00406  5504 
00407  5505     N1 correction 17 (M2): the construction of the chain is **inside**
00408  5506     the guard of the phase, the barrier of the publication is waited
00409  5507     for **after** the cause of the coordination - never before it - and
00410  5508     the facts of the barrier are read from the **persisted** snapshot of
00411  5509     the seam.  A phase that was **executed** and that failed is a
00412  5510     **FAIL** with its raw facts; only a phase that was never entered is
00413  5511     a ``NOT_RUN``.  The result of the phase is written **last**, after
00414  5512     the two real stops and after the cleanup of the phase.
00415  5513     """

00478  5576     def record_guarded(name, facts):
00479  5577         """Write one document and **never** replace an original failure.

00481  5579         CORRECTION 18 (M2): the writing of the evidence of a phase that
00482  5580         is already failing must never replace the original failure: the
00483  5581         error of the write is retained in ``write_errors`` and the phase
00484  5582         fails **closed**.

00487  5585             return record(name, facts)
00488  5586         except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00489  5587             write_errors.append({'name': name,
00490  5588                                  'type': type(error).__name__,
00491  5589                                  'detail': str(error)})
00492  5590             _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00493  5591             return None

01053  6151 class _M09Gate:
01054  6152     """The transparent gate of the wait of the worker.
01055  6153 
01056  6154     The gate is a **wrapper** of the production wait of the worker: it
01057  6155     calls the **original** wait and it holds the endpoint **after** that
01058  6156     wait returned and **before** the endpoint rechecks or consumes the
01059  6157     outcome of its own generation.
01060  6158 
01061  6159     The gate never decides the outcome, never rewrites the history of
01062  6160     the error, never touches the selection of the error of the endpoint
01063  6161     and never returns a fact of its own: it only decides **when** the
01064  6162     endpoint continues.  Every value that the node asserts afterwards is
01065  6163     a value that the production returned.
01066  6164 
01067  6165     The gate holds **one named worker** and it holds it only while the
01068  6166     read of the round is really in flight: the frames of the start of
01069  6167     the round are never held and the write of the round is never held.
01070  6168     """
01071  6169 
01072  6170     def __init__(self, api):
01073  6171         self.api = api
01074  6172         self.entered = threading.Event()
01075  6173         self.release = threading.Event()
01076  6174         self.calls = []
01077  6175         self.target = None
01078  6176         self.armed = True
01079  6177 
01080  6178     def install(self, worker_class):
01081  6179         """Wrap the production wait of the worker class."""
01082  6180         original = worker_class.wait_done
01083  6181         gate = self
01084  6182 
01085  6183         def gated_wait_done(worker, generation, timeout):
01086  6184             result = original(worker, generation, timeout)
01087  6185             gate.calls.append({'generation': generation,
01088  6186                                'timeout': timeout,
01089  6187                                'result': bool(result)})
01090  6188             if (gate.armed and not result and worker is gate.target
01091  6189                     and gate.api.read_waiting.is_set()):
01092  6190                 # The endpoint is held **after** the production wait and
01093  6191                 # **before** it rechecks its generation.
01094  6192                 gate.entered.set()
01095  6193                 gate.release.wait(30.0)
01096  6194             return result
01097  6195 
01098  6196         worker_class.wait_done = gated_wait_done
01099  6197         return original

01102  6200 def _wait_for_outcome(worker, generation, seconds):
01103  6201     """The immutable outcome of **that** generation of the worker.
01104  6202 
01105  6203     The generic event of the worker may be stale: the event is only a
01106  6204     wake up and the **outcome of the named generation** is the fact that
01107  6205     the wait is really about.
01108  6206     """
01109  6207     deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
01110  6208     while time.monotonic() < deadline:
01111  6209         outcome = worker.outcome(generation)
01112  6210         if outcome is not None and outcome.get('error') is not None:
01113  6211             return outcome
01114  6212         worker.outcome_published.wait(0.05)
01115  6213     return None

01118  6216 def _wait_for_missing_outcome(worker, generation, seconds):
01119  6217     """Wait, bounded, for the outcome of a generation that never existed.
01120  6218 
01121  6219     The wait is the **negative** of the barrier of the publication: the
01122  6220     outcome of that generation is never published, the wait ends with
01123  6221     ``None`` and it never decides an outcome, never writes one and
01124  6222     never replaces the error of the round.
01125  6223     """
01126  6224     deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
01127  6225     while time.monotonic() < deadline:
01128  6226         outcome = worker.outcome(generation)
01129  6227         if outcome is not None:
01130  6228             return outcome

01132  6230     return None

01135  6233 def _m09_published_fault_phase(document, plan, tmp_path, *, phase,
01136  6234                                inventory=None, ledger=None):
01137  6235     """The schedule that the contract requires: the fault comes first.
01138  6236 
01139  6237     The ordinary failure of the read is published **before** the
01140  6238     effective timeout of the round arrives and the endpoint consumes the
01141  6239     outcome of its generation only **after** the timeout was decided.
01142  6240 
01143  6241     The order that is driven and recorded is therefore
01144  6242 
01145  6243         the publication of the fault -> the immutable outcome of that
01146  6244         generation exists -> the effective timeout arrives -> the
01147  6245         endpoint consumes the outcome.
01148  6246

01150  6248     wait of the worker: it calls the original wait and it holds the

01153  6251     the **named** generation is waited for (the generic event of the
01154  6252     worker may be stale) and the timeout of the round is advanced only
01155  6253     after the outcome really exists.

01598  6696 def test_n10_r10_the_outcome_of_the_generation_wins_over_the_cancellation(tmp_path):
01599  6697     """N10-R10 (M09): a real fault of the round is never a benign cancel.
01600  6698 
01601  6699     Obligation: the worker of an endpoint keeps the **outcome** of
01602  6700     every generation it runs: the result, the error, the original error
01603  6701     object and the order of the completion.  A failure that was really
01604  6702     published **before** the cancellation of the round is the first
01605  6703     error of the round: a close that sets the cancel flag afterwards
01606  6704     may not replace it and it may not turn it into a benign
01607  6705     cancellation.  The identity of the token of the cancel is not a

01609  6707     reader is a **history**: two real stops of the round keep it and

01611  6709 
01612  6710     Entry: ``_WindowsPipeWorker.outcome``,

01627  6725     CORRECTION 11 (M09): the outcome of the **same** generation is

01701  6799

01709  6807

00361 +class _StartObserver:

00412 +class _PhaseLedger:
00413 +    """The ledger of the phases that the group of this module runs.
00414 +
00415 +    The ledger remembers what was **entered** and what **ended**.  It
00416 +    never decides: a phase that was entered and that failed is a
00417 +    ``FAIL`` and only a phase that was never entered is a ``NOT_RUN``.
00418 +    The states are ``PLANNED``, ``ATTEMPTED``, ``PASSED``, ``FAIL`` and
00419 +    ``NOT_RUN`` and the two last states are terminal.
00420 +    """
00421 +
00422 +    STATES = ('PLANNED', 'ATTEMPTED', 'PASSED', 'FAIL', 'NOT_RUN')
00423 +
00424 +    def __init__(self):
00425 +        self._lock = threading.Lock()
00426 +        self._states = {}
00427 +        self._order = []
00428 +        self._reasons = {}
00429 +
00430 +    def _plan_locked(self, name):
00431 +        if name not in self._states:
00432 +            self._states[name] = 'PLANNED'
00433 +            self._order.append(name)
00434 +
00435 +    def plan(self, name):
00436 +        """Name one phase **before** it runs."""
00437 +        with self._lock:
00438 +            self._plan_locked(name)
00439 +            return name
00440 +
00441 +    def attempt(self, name):
00442 +        """Mark that the operation of the phase was **entered**."""
00443 +        with self._lock:
00444 +            self._plan_locked(name)
00445 +            if self._states[name] == 'PLANNED':
00446 +                self._states[name] = 'ATTEMPTED'
00447 +            return self._states[name]
00448 +
00449 +    def finish(self, name, state, reason=None):
00450 +        """Close one phase; a closed phase is never reopened."""
00451 +        with self._lock:
00452 +            self._plan_locked(name)
00453 +            if self._states[name] in ('PASSED', 'FAIL', 'NOT_RUN'):
00454 +                return self._states[name]
00455 +            self._states[name] = state
00456 +            if reason is not None:
00457 +                self._reasons[name] = reason
00458 +            return state
00459 +
00460 +    def pass_(self, name):
00461 +        """The phase held every one of its checks."""
00462 +        return self.finish(name, 'PASSED')
00463 +
00464 +    def fail(self, name, reason=None):
00465 +        """The phase was executed and it failed."""
00466 +        return self.finish(name, 'FAIL', reason)
00467 +
00468 +    def state(self, name):
00469 +        """The state of one phase."""
00470 +        with self._lock:
00471 +            return self._states.get(name, 'PLANNED')
00472 +
00473 +    def names(self):
00474 +        """The names of the phases in the order of their planning."""
00475 +        with self._lock:
00476 +            return list(self._order)
00477 +
00478 +    def reason(self, name):
00479 +        """The reason of the failure of one phase."""
00480 +        with self._lock:
00481 +            return self._reasons.get(name)

00918 +def _registry_owners(registry, session=None, channel=None, prefix='round',
00919 +                      errors=None, interrupts=None):
00920 +    """Every owner of the round: the registered ones and the live ones.
00921 +
00922 +    The registry of the fixture holds the owners that were registered
00923 +    **immediately** - a channel that was constructed, an endpoint that
00924 +    was built, a session that was created.  The session and the
00925 +    channel that are still reachable are added to them, so that a
00926 +    thread that the product started after the registration is never
00927 +    forgotten.  One owner is never in the list twice: the identity of
00928 +    the thread decides and not its name.
00929 +
00930 +    CORRECTION 19 (M3): the traversal is **best effort**.  The query
00931 +    of one container never aborts the traversal and it never replaces
00932 +    the owners of the round with an empty list: every other owner is
00933 +    still attempted.  The **exact** thread objects that the start
00934 +    registry observed are retained **first** and they are an
00935 +    independent fallback - a failure of the query of a container never
00936 +    loses them.  Every failure is retained with its exact type and its
00937 +    exact detail and the **exact** object of an interruption is kept.
00938 +    """
00939 +    owners = []
00940 +    hints = {}
00941 +    seen = set()
00942 +    kinds = set()
00943 +
00944 +    def add(items):
00945 +        for name, thread in items:
00946 +            key = ('thread', id(thread)) if thread is not None \
00947 +                else ('name', name)
00948 +            if key in seen:
00949 +                continue
00950 +            seen.add(key)
00951 +            owners.append((name, thread))
00952 +
00953 +    def note(kind, error):
00954 +        """Retain one failure of the traversal, never swallow it."""
00955 +        if errors is not None:
00956 +            errors.append({'kind': kind, 'type': type(error).__name__,
00957 +                           'detail': str(error)})
00958 +        _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
00959 +
00960 +    try:
00961 +        entries = registry.entries()
00962 +    except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00963 +        note('REGISTRY_ENTRIES', error)
00964 +        entries = []
00965 +    # CORRECTION 19 (M3): the **exact** thread objects that the start
00966 +    # registry observed are retained **first** and they are an
00967 +    # independent fallback: a failure of the query of a container never
00968 +    # loses them and it never replaces the owners of the round with an
00969 +    # empty list.  They are merged into the owners **after** the
00970 +    # traversal, so that the name of an owner that a container really
00971 +    # knows is never replaced by the name of the registry.
00972 +    observed = [(item.get('name'), item.get('owner'))
00973 +                for item in entries
00974 +                if item.get('kind') == 'thread'
00975 +                and item.get('owner') is not None]
00976 +    for entry in entries:
00977 +        name = entry.get('name')
00978 +        owner = entry.get('owner')
00979 +        kind = entry.get('kind')
00980 +        if kind == 'thread':
00981 +            add([(name, owner)])
00982 +            continue
00983 +        try:
00984 +            if kind == 'channel':
00985 +                items = _channel_owners(owner, name, hints)
00986 +            elif kind == 'endpoint':
00987 +                items = _endpoint_owners(name, owner, hints)
00988 +            elif kind == 'session':
00989 +                items = _session_owners(owner, name, hints)
00990 +            else:
00991 +                items = [(name, owner)]
00992 +        except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
00993 +            # the traversal continues: the owners that follow this one
00994 +            # are still attempted and the exact thread object of this
00995 +            # entry is still an owner of the round.
00996 +            note('OWNER_QUERY', error)
00997 +            if isinstance(owner, threading.Thread):
00998 +                add([(name, owner)])
00999 +            continue
01000 +        kinds.add(kind)
01001 +        add(items)
01002 +    try:
01003 +        if session is not None and 'session' not in kinds:
01004 +            add(_session_owners(session, '%s:session' % prefix, hints))
01005 +    except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
01006 +        note('SESSION_QUERY', error)
01007 +    try:
01008 +        if channel is not None and 'channel' not in kinds:
01009 +            add(_channel_owners(channel, '%s:channel' % prefix, hints))
01010 +    except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
01011 +        note('CHANNEL_QUERY', error)
01012 +    # CORRECTION 19 (M3): the fallback of the observed threads: every
01013 +    # exact thread object that the start registry saw is an owner of the
01014 +    # round.  The merge is **idempotent**: an owner that the traversal
01015 +    # already named keeps its name and its hint.
01016 +    for name, thread in observed:
01017 +        add([(name, thread)])
01018 +    # CORRECTION 17 (M3): the provenance of the starts that the
01019 +    # observer of the fixture saw is the **proven** provenance of the
01020 +    # start of an owner.  It is keyed by the exact thread object and it
01021 +    # never replaces the hint of the production: a thread whose start
01022 +    # returned is ``STARTED`` and a thread whose start did not return is
01023 +    # ``UNKNOWN``.
01024 +    try:

01027 +        note('PROVENANCE', error)
01028 +        provenance = {}
01029 +    for name, thread in owners:
01030 +        if thread is None:
01031 +            continue
01032 +        state = provenance.get(id(thread))
01033 +        if state == 'STARTED':
01034 +            hints[name] = 'STARTED'
01035 +        elif state in ('STARTING', 'FAILED'):

01040 +def _drain_owners(registry, session=None, channel=None, prefix='round', *,
01041 +                  seconds=10.0, budget=30.0, release=None, interrupts=None):
01042 +    """The bounded drain of the owners of one round.
01043 +
01044 +    CORRECTION 17 (M3): the drain repeats, **boundedly**, until the
01045 +    owners of the round are quiescent and really joined.  The bound of
01046 +    the drain is **one** overall bound: the wait of an owner is cropped
01047 +    by the remaining budget and the budget is never reset - neither
01048 +    between the rounds of the drain nor between the rounds of the test.
01049 +
01050 +    The quiescence of the round is asserted **after** the drain and
01051 +    never before it: a round that is not quiescent is a failure of the
01052 +    cleanup, the gates of the round are still released and **all** the
01053 +    registered owners are still attempted.
01054 +

01060 +    readings must agree and the **final** exact-owner resnapshot must

01069 +    is kept: an error of an earlier iteration is never erased by a
01070 +    later iteration that really ended the threads.  A failure never
01071 +    aborts the iteration and it never skips the final result of the
01072 +    round.  The drain never renews a deadline of the product.
01073 +
01074 +    CORRECTION 19 (M3): every read of the drain - the generation, the
01075 +    pending starts and the final resnapshot - is **best effort** and it
01076 +    never skips the owners that follow it.  The release of the gates is
01077 +    **one action per gate**: a failure of one gate never skips the gate

01099 +            return registry.generation()

01101 +            errors.append({'kind': label, 'type': type(error).__name__,
01102 +                           'detail': str(error)})
01103 +            _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
01104 +            return None
01105 +
01106 +    def read_pending(label):
01107 +        """Read the pending starts of the registry, guarded."""
01108 +        try:
01109 +            return registry.pending_starts()
01110 +        except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
01111 +            errors.append({'kind': label, 'type': type(error).__name__,
01112 +                           'detail': str(error)})
01113 +            _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
01114 +            return None
01115 +
01116 +    while True:
01117 +        # the generation of the registry is read **before** the exact
01118 +        # owners are enumerated
01119 +        generation_before = read_generation('GENERATION_BEFORE')
01120 +        try:
01121 +            owners, hints = _registry_owners(registry, session=session,
01122 +                                              channel=channel, prefix=prefix,
01123 +                                              errors=errors,
01124 +                                              interrupts=interrupts)
01125 +        except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
01126 +            errors.append({'kind': 'ENUMERATION',
01127 +                           'type': type(error).__name__,
01128 +                           'detail': str(error)})
01129 +            _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
01130 +            # CORRECTION 19 (M3): the owners of the previous observation
01131 +            # are **retained**: a failure of the enumeration never loses
01132 +            # them and it never replaces them with an empty list.
01133 +        # ... and it is read **again** right after the enumeration: a
01134 +        # start that happened between the two readings is a change of
01135 +        # the generation and the enumeration is repeated.
01136 +        generation_after = read_generation('GENERATION_AFTER')
01137 +        snapshot = {'generation_before': generation_before,
01138 +                    'generation_after': generation_after,
01139 +                    'generation': generation_after,
01140 +                    'pending': read_pending('PENDING'),
01141 +                    'owners': [name for name, _ in owners],
01142 +                    'errors': list(errors)}
01143 +        attempts.append(snapshot)
01144 +        if release is not None:
01145 +            # CORRECTION 19 (M3): the release of the gates is **best
01146 +            # effort**: every gate is released on its own and a failure
01147 +            # of one gate never skips the gate that follows it.
01148 +            actions = (release if isinstance(release, (list, tuple))
01149 +                       else [release])

01161 +                                   interrupts=interrupts)

01163 +        # the failure of an earlier iteration is never erased by a later

01174 +        except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - it stays visible
01175 +            errors.append({'kind': 'FINAL_ENUMERATION',
01176 +                           'type': type(error).__name__,
01177 +                           'detail': str(error)})
01178 +            _note_interruption(interrupts, error)
01179 +            final_owners = []
01180 +        # and the generation is read **again** after the final
01181 +        # resnapshot: a start that happened during it is a change of the
01182 +        # generation and the drain repeats.
01183 +        final_generation_after = read_generation('FINAL_GENERATION_AFTER')
01184 +        final_names = [name for name, _ in final_owners]
01185 +        missing = [name for name in snapshot['owners']

01187 +        late = [name for name in final_names
01188 +                if name not in snapshot['owners']]

01191 +                  and final_generation == generation_after

01194 +        quiescent = (pending == 0 and stable

01196 +        if quiescent or time.monotonic() >= deadline:
01197 +            break
