21194 ## 2. M1 — the public zero-admission chain (test module only)
21195 
21196 ### 2.1 C1 — the malformed patch (the review's trigger 1)
21197 
21198 **Current (T10:2676-2677):**
21199 
21200 ```python
21201 with unittest.mock.patch.object(broker_module, 'BrokerProcess',
21202                                 'read', zero_gated_broker_read), \
21203      unittest.mock.patch.object(custody_module, '_ReplyWaiter',
21204                                 ZeroTighteningWaiter):
21205 ```
21206 
21207 `unittest.mock.patch.object(target, attribute, new, spec, ...)` — the third
21208 positional argument is **`new`**, not a spec. The call therefore assigns the
21209 **string** `'read'` to the *module* attribute `BrokerProcess`; the real class
21210 is never patched, `B:7896` then tries to call that string, the launcher
21211 failure is swallowed by `C:1744-1756` and the round returns a structured
21212 failure — so **no** attached pump and **no** public reply admission is ever
21213 created for the zero round. This is a static control/data-flow conclusion; no
21214 runtime failure is claimed here.
21215 
21216 **Proposed (C1):** patch the **class method** with the class as the target:
21217 
21218 ```python
21219 with unittest.mock.patch.object(broker_module.BrokerProcess, 'read',
21220                                 zero_gated_broker_read), \
21221      unittest.mock.patch.object(custody_module, '_ReplyWaiter',
21222                                 ZeroTighteningWaiter):
21223 ```
21224 
21225 * `zero_gated_broker_read(self, timeout)` (`T10:2610-2624`) keeps the
21226   **original signature** of `BrokerProcess.read` (`B:6467-6468`:
21227   `def read(self, timeout): return self._channel.read(timeout)`), so the
21228   replacement is a plain function installed on the class and it is called as
21229   `broker.read(timeout)` → `zero_gated_broker_read(broker, timeout)`.
21230 * The replacement **forwards** the original unbound method
21231   (`zero_original_broker_read = broker_module.BrokerProcess.read`, captured
21232   at `T10:2590` **before** the patch) → `zero_original_broker_read(self, timeout)`.
21233   The original result is returned unchanged.
21234 * The gate is **round-scoped**: it only holds the broker whose
21235   `self._context is zero_session._context`; every other broker keeps the
21236   original behaviour (`T10:2618-2619`).
21237 * The `_ReplyWaiter` patch is unchanged: `custody_module._ReplyWaiter`
21238   (`C:764`) is looked up at **call time** inside `_ChannelPump.take`
21239   (`C:895`), so the patch really intercepts the waiter that the **public**
21240   start builds (`C:1784`, `C:1793`).
21241 
21242 **Scope / max wait / negative oracle:** the patch lives only inside the
21243 zero-round `with` block (`T10:2675-2685`) and is removed by the context
21244 manager. The gate wait is bounded by `ZERO_GATE_SECONDS = 30.0`
21245 (`T10:145`); the admission wait is bounded by `ZERO_ADMISSION_SECONDS = 15.0`
21246 (`T10:146`). Negative oracle: if the gate is never reached, `zero_gate_facts`
21247 is empty → `C7`/`Z10` fails with *"the admission of the zero round never
21248 reached the gate"*; if the gate timed out, `zero_gate_facts[0]['released'] is
21249 False` → *"the gate of the admission of the zero round timed out"*.
21250 
21251 ### 2.2 C2 — the actual error value vs. its display `repr`
21252 
21253 **Current:** `T10:2650-2651` stores `repr(pump.error)` into
21254 `zero_premise['pump_error_at_admission']` and `T10:2705-2706` stores
21255 `repr(zero_pump.error)` into the facts; `T10:2733` then requires that stored
21256 value to `is None`. A healthy pump has `error is None`, so `repr(None)` is the
21257 **string** `'None'` and the premise can never hold.
21258 
21259 **Proposed (C2):** keep the *display* form for the human-readable document but
21260 store the **actual** value separately, and assert on the actual value:
21261 
21262 | key | value | use |
21263 |---|---|---|
21264 | `pump_error_is_none` | `pump.error is None` (a real `bool`) | the assertion oracle |
21265 | `pump_error_type` | `type(pump.error).__name__` or `None` | the failure name |
21266 | `pump_error_repr` | `repr(pump.error)` or `None` | the display form only, **never** an oracle |
21267 
21268 `T10:2733` becomes
21269 `assert zero_premise['pump_error_is_none'] is True` (plus
21270 `assert zero_premise['pump_error_repr'] is None` as the redundant display
21271 check). The same split is applied to the facts document at `T10:2705-2706`
21272 (`zero_pump_error_is_none`, `zero_pump_error_type`, `zero_pump_error_repr`).
21273 
21274 ### 2.3 C3/C4 — the **actual** public start return
21275 
21276 `NativeCustodySession.start()` (`C:1709-1818`) **returns** `self.evidence()`
21277 (`C:1808`, `C:1750`, `C:1754`, `C:1780`, `C:1798`) and never raises for an
21278 ordinary failure. The fixture's `start_round` (`T10:2314-2352`) calls
21279 `round_session.start()` at `T10:2347` and **discards** the return, returning
21280 the session object instead (`T10:2352`); `T10:2689` then re-reads
21281 `zero_session.evidence()` — a *later* evidence object, not the one the public
21282 operation returned.
21283 
21284 **Proposed (C3):** `start_round` keeps its arguments and captures the public
21285 return value:
21286 
21287 ```python
21288 start_return = round_session.start()      # the ACTUAL return of the public start
21289 ...
21290 return start_return                        # the return of the helper
21291 ```
21292 
21293 All three call sites bind it:
21294 
21295 * `T10:2371` → `parent_start_return = start_round(session, api, clock, parent_registry)`
21296 * `T10:2682` → `zero_start_return = start_round(zero_session, zero_api, zero_clock, zero_registry)`
21297 * `T10:3221` → `controlled_start_return = start_round(controlled_session, controlled_api, controlled_clock, controlled_registry)`
21298 
21299 (The helper returns the start result instead of the session; the session
21300 object itself is already in scope at every call site, so no other use is
21301 lost.)
21302 
21303 **Proposed (C4):** the zero round uses the **captured return** as the returned
21304 state of the product — `zero_returned = zero_start_return` — and the later
21305 `zero_session.evidence()` is used only as a **cross-check** that the state
21306 did not change after the return (`zero_session.evidence()['state'] ==
21307 zero_start_return['state']`). The original failure is never overwritten by the
21308 later read.
21309 
21310 ### 2.4 C5 — the actual public start / retention oracle
21311 
21312 `evidence()` always supplies the key `broker_retained` (`C:2361`), so a
21313 key-presence check (`T10:2772`) proves nothing. The **value** of the
21314 retention and the **identity** of the retained resource are the oracle.
21315 
21316 | id | oracle (exact predicate) | fact source | failure message |
21317 |---|---|---|---|
21318 | **Z1** | `zero_start_return['state'] == 'UNKNOWN_RETAINED'` | the value returned by the public `start` | *the public start of the zero round did not latch its state* |
21319 | **Z2** | `'CUSTODY_CHANNEL_TIMEOUT' in zero_start_return['failures']` | same return (`C:1812-1813`) | *the public start of the zero round did not name the timeout of the admission* |
21320 | **Z3** | `'CUSTODY_CHANNEL_EOF' not in zero_start_return['failures']` | same return | *the round ended at the end of the stream instead of the timeout* |
21321 | **Z4** | `zero_start_return['broker_retained'] is True` | same return (`C:2361`) | *the round did not retain its broker* |
21322 | **Z5** | `zero_broker is not None and zero_session.broker is zero_broker` | the live attribute (`C:991`, `C:1741`) and the object of the round | *the retained original resource is not the object of the round* |
21323 | **Z6** | `zero_start_return['broker']['identity_source'] == 'PARENT_ORIGINAL_HANDLE'` **and** `zero_start_return['broker']['pid'] == zero_broker.pid` | same return (`C:1755-1761`) | *the identity of the broker is a claim and not the original handle* |
21324 | **Z7** | `zero_start_return['pump_error'] is None` | same return (`C:2365-2367`) | *the pump of the round failed before the admission* |
21325 | **Z8** | `zero_pump is zero_session._pump` **and** `zero_pump._context is zero_session._context` **and** `zero_pump.finished is True` | the **attached** pump (`C:1772`, `C:1782`) | *the attached pump of the zero round is not the pump of the session / did not end / has another context* |
21326 | **Z9** | `zero_queue_waits[-1] == 0.0` **and** `zero_reply_waits[-1] == 0.0` | the **actual arguments** the production passed (`T10:2604`, `T10:2663`) | *the round asked for a wait after the expiry* |
21327 | **Z10** | `zero_gate_facts` non-empty **and** `zero_gate_facts[0]['released'] is True` **and** `zero_gate_facts[0]['timeout'] == ZERO_GATE_SECONDS` | the recorded gate facts (`T10:2622-2623`) | *the gate of the admission of the zero round timed out* |
21328 | **Z11** | the recorded order of §2.5 | the order trace | *the order of the start, the pump, the queue, the reply and the gate was not the required one* |
21329 | **Z12** | `_assert_salvage_proved(zero_salvage, 'the round of zero')` | the salvage facts | *an owner of the zero round was left behind* |
21330 
21331 Z1–Z3 are the **exact cause** of the failure (the timeout, not the EOF, not a
21332 launcher refusal); Z4–Z6 are the **actual retention** (value + identity of
21333 the retained original resource); Z8–Z10 are the **bounded, checked**
21334 no-EOF / timeout facts; Z11 is the ordering; Z12 is the bounded cleanup.
21335 
21336 ### 2.5 C6/C7 — the actual ordering, with the bounded checked no-EOF/timeouts
21337 
21338 A single ordered trace is recorded during the zero round. Every event is
21339 appended **at the moment it happens**, by the transparent seam, with its
21340 actual argument:
21341 
21342 | id | event | recorded at | recorded argument |
21343 |---|---|---|---|
21344 | **E1** | `START_CALLED` | `start_round`, immediately **before** `round_session.start()` | — |
21345 | **E2** | `PUMP_READ_ENTERED` | `zero_gated_broker_read`, before the gate wait (`T10:2620`) | the `timeout` the production passed |
21346 | **E3** | `REPLY_WAIT_ENTERED` | `ZeroTighteningWaiter.recording_wait`, before the original wait (`T10:2664`) | the `timeout` the production passed |
21347 | **E4** | `REPLY_WAIT_RETURNED` | immediately **after** the original wait returned and **before** `zero_gate.set()` (`T10:2665-2670`) | the original result (`False` at the zero expiry) |
21348 | **E5** | `GATE_RELEASED` | `zero_gated_broker_read`, after `zero_gate.wait(...)` returned (`T10:2621-2623`) | `released` / `timeout` |
21349 | **E6** | `QUEUE_GET_ENTERED` | `zero_recording_get` (`T10:2604-2606`) | the **actual** `timeout` the production passed to the queue |
21350 | **E7** | `PUMP_ENDED` | the observation loop (`T10:2696-2700`) | `zero_pump.finished` |
21351 
21352 **Required order (the assertion of Z11):**
21353 `E1 < E2 < E3 < E4 < E5 < E6 < E7`.
21354 
21355 * `E2 < E3` — the waiter of the reply is built by the admission of the public
21356   start (`C:895`) and its constructor waits for `zero_held`
21357   (`T10:2644-2645`), which is set inside the held read (`T10:2620`).
21358 * `E4 < E5` — the gate is released by the reply waiter **after** the reply
21359   wait returned (`T10:2666-2670`); the pump is therefore still held while the
21360   reply admission completes, and the end of the stream / the error of the
21361   pump can never preempt the reply the round owes.
21362 * `E5 < E6` — the attached pump performs its real read of the channel
21363   (`B:5496-5529`) only after the gate was released.
21364 * `E6 < E7` — the pump really ends.
21365 
21366 **Bounded, checked no-EOF / timeout facts (recorded and asserted):**
21367 
21368 | id | check | source | bound |
21369 |---|---|---|---|
21370 | **N1** | `zero_premise['pump_eof_at_admission'] is False` — the pump was **not** at the end of its stream when the admission began | `T10:2648-2649` (`pump._eof`) | — |
21371 | **N2** | the failure cause is the **timeout** and not the EOF (Z2 + Z3) — the round really failed on the admission, not on an early end of stream | `C:1874-1890` (the code of the failure) | — |
21372 | **N3** | every queue wait recorded **after** `E5` has `timeout == 0.0` — a round whose bound arrived asks for nothing (`B:5513-5520`) | `T10:2604-2606` | ≤ the recorded arguments |
21373 | **N4** | the reply wait of the admission asked for `0.0` (`C:910-921`: `remaining = limit - clock()`) | `T10:2663-2664` | — |
21374 | **N5** | the gate wait is bounded by `ZERO_GATE_SECONDS` and the recorded `released` flag proves it did not time out | `T10:2621-2623` | 30.0 s |
21375 | **N6** | the admission wait is bounded by `ZERO_ADMISSION_SECONDS` | `T10:2644-2645` | 15.0 s |
21376 | **N7** | the observation loops are bounded (`T10:2696-2700`, `T10:2814-2818`) | — | 15.0 s each |
21377 
21378 ### 2.6 Exception boundaries of the zero block (M1)
21379 
21380 The zero block keeps **one** `try/finally` whose `finally` owns the salvage
21381 (`T10:2775-2796`), and the boundary is explicit:
21382 
21383 * **Inside** the `try`: the public start, the observation of the attached
21384   pump, the durable document `r07-zero-public-chain` and the assertions Z1–Z11.
21385 * **Inside** the `finally`: `zero_gate.set()` and `zero_api.frames_ready.set()`
21386   (the gates are released **unconditionally**), then `_capture_stop`,
21387   `_registry_owners`, `_salvage_threads`, `_prove_salvage`, the durable
21388   document `r07-zero-salvage`, and the raising of the proof failure **only**
21389   when no other failure is unwinding (`sys.exc_info()[0] is None`).
21390 * **Never** inside: a `try/except` that swallows the failure of the public
21391   start. The public start returns a structured failure instead of raising
21392   (`C:1744-1756`, `C:1806-1817`) — the design therefore asserts on the
21393   **returned** value, and it does not convert a refusal into a skip.
21394

21396 
21397 ## 3. M2 — truthful phase inventory, FAIL vs NOT_RUN, durable barrier
21398 
21399 ### 3.1 C8 — the attempt ledger (one small local helper)
21400 
21401 A module-level ledger, used by the two M09 phase helpers and by the outer
21402 `test_n10_r10` test:
21403 
21404 ```
21405 _PHASE_STATES = ('PLANNED', 'ATTEMPTED', 'PASSED', 'FAIL', 'NOT_RUN')
21406 
21407 class _PhaseLedger:
21408     def plan(self, name):        # named before it runs
21409     def attempt(self, name):     # AT THE MOMENT the operation is entered
21410     def pass_(self, name):       # only after every assertion of it held
21411     def fail(self, name, reason):# it was attempted and it failed
21412     def state(self, name):       # PLANNED / ATTEMPTED / PASSED / FAIL
21413     def names(self):             # in the frozen order
21414 ```
21415 
21416 The ledger is **not** a framework: it is one small class next to
21417 `_OwnerRegistry` (`T10:214-254`) with the same shape (a lock + a list) and
21418 the same purpose (remembering, never deciding).
21419 
21420 ### 3.2 State-transition table
21421 
21422 | from | event | to | durable document |
21423 |---|---|---|---|
21424 | `PLANNED` | the operation is **entered** (`attempt()` — called *before* the construction, the phase body or the stop call) | `ATTEMPTED` | none yet |
21425 | `PLANNED` | the end of the test, the operation was never entered | `NOT_RUN` | `{'status': 'NOT_RUN', 'reason': <type of the first failure>}` — **no facts of the phase** |
21426 | `ATTEMPTED` | the raw facts are written (durable, before the assertions) | `ATTEMPTED` (unchanged) | `{'status': 'EXECUTED', ...raw facts...}` |
21427 | `ATTEMPTED` | every assertion of the operation held | `PASSED` | rewrite of the same path: `{'status': 'PASSED', ...raw facts...}` |
21428 | `ATTEMPTED` | an assertion raised **or** the operation itself raised | `FAIL` | rewrite of the same path: `{'status': 'FAIL', 'executed': True, 'reason': <type>, 'detail': <str>, ...raw facts...}` |
21429 | `PASSED` / `FAIL` / `NOT_RUN` | anything | unchanged (**terminal**) | never overwritten by the inventory |
21430 
21431 ### 3.3 Document lifecycle table
21432 
21433 | document | written when | final status written by |
21434 |---|---|---|
21435 | `<phase>-barrier` | **before** the first assertion that depends on the barrier | the phase (PASSED) or the failure handler (FAIL) |
21436 | `<phase>` | the raw facts, **before** the assertions | the phase (PASSED) or the failure handler (FAIL) |
21437 | `<phase>-first` / `<phase>-second` | right after the corresponding **actual** stop returned | the phase (PASSED) or the failure handler (FAIL) — an **attempted** stop that raises is FAIL, never NOT_RUN |
21438 
21439 `write_phase` (`T10:149-155`) overwrites the file at the same path, so the
21440 "raw facts" write and the "final status" write are the **same** document:
21441 the final status never erases the raw facts, it adds the verdict.
21442 
21443 ### 3.4 C9 — a document is marked *written* only **after** persistence succeeded
21444 
21445 **Current (`T10:4104-4116` and `T10:4458-4463`):**
21446 
21447 ```python
21448 def record(name, facts):
21449     written.add(name)                 # marked BEFORE the write
21450     if inventory is not None:
21451         inventory.add(name)            # marked BEFORE the write
21452     return write_phase(name, facts)
21453 ```
21454 
21455 A `write_phase` that raises (disk error, encoding error) leaves the name
21456 marked as written although no document exists.
21457 
21458 **Proposed (C9):**
21459 
21460 ```python
21461 def record(name, facts):
21462     path = write_phase(name, facts)    # the persistence FIRST
21463     written.add(name)                  # marked only after it succeeded
21464     if inventory is not None:
21465         inventory.add(name)
21466     ledger.pass_or_fail(name, ...)     # the ledger follows the same rule
21467     return path
21468 ```
21469 
21470 The `written` set and the inventory are then a **reliable** membership test
21471 for "a document exists on disk".
21472 
21473 ### 3.5 C10 — `_m09_timeout_phase` (`T10:4032-4329`)
21474 
21475 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D1, D2, D5, D6).** The shape below is
21476 > superseded by §10.2 (the causal order of the barrier), §10.3 (the
21477 > construction inside the local guard, the phase result document and the
21478 > whole-test guard) and §10.6 (the transitions). The pseudocode below is kept
21479 > only as the shape of the helper; **the ordering of the barrier wait and the
21480 > inventory/result rules of §10 are authoritative**.
21481 
21482 Proposed shape (pseudocode; the production is untouched):
21483 
21484 ```python
21485 def _m09_timeout_phase(document, plan, tmp_path, *, phase, confirm_the_worker,
21486                         hold_the_worker, barrier_probe='EXACT',
21487                         expect_barrier='PASSED', inventory=None, ledger=None):
21488     ledger.plan(phase); ledger.plan(phase+'-barrier')
21489     ledger.plan(phase+'-first'); ledger.plan(phase+'-second')
21490     api = _M09TimeoutApi(confirm_the_worker=confirm_the_worker,
21491                          hold_the_worker=hold_the_worker)
21492     api.barrier_probe = barrier_probe
21493     ledger.attempt(phase + '-construction')          # BEFORE the construction
21494     session, holder, channel_closes, channel_facts = _chain(
21495         api, document, plan, tmp_path, clock=clock)
21496     worker = None
21497     raw = {}                                          # the raw facts per document
21498     try:
21499         ledger.attempt(phase)
21500         session.start()
21501         # -- a WAIT, not an assertion: the barrier announces itself ----
21502         if expect_barrier in ('PASSED', 'REFUSED'):
21503             api.barrier_entered.wait(15.0)             # bounded wait
21504         barrier = dict(api.barrier)                   # the ACTUAL facts
21505         raw[phase + '-barrier'] = {...}                # the facts of the barrier
21506         record(phase + '-barrier', {'status': 'EXECUTED', 'barrier': barrier,
21507                                      'barrier_expectation': expect_barrier, ...})
21508         # -- only NOW the assertions of the phase ------------------------
21509         assert api.read_waiting.wait(15.0), ...
21510         ...
21511         record(phase, {'status': 'EXECUTED', **raw[phase]})
21512         assert <the assertions of the phase>
21513         ledger.pass_(phase)
21514         record(phase, {'status': 'PASSED', **raw[phase]})     # the rewrite
21515         # -- the FIRST real stop ----------------------------------------
21516         ledger.attempt(phase + '-first')
21517         first = session.stop()                        # a raise here => FAIL
21518         raw[phase+'-first'] = {...}
21519         record(phase+'-first', {'status': 'EXECUTED', **raw[phase+'-first']})
21520         assert first_facts.get('channel_reader_error') == 'RuntimeError', ...
21521         assert first['broker_retained'] is True
21522         assert first['state'] == 'UNKNOWN_RETAINED'
21523         ledger.pass_(phase+'-first')
21524         record(phase+'-first', {'status': 'PASSED', **raw[phase+'-first']})
21525         # -- the SECOND real stop ---------------------------------------
21526         ledger.attempt(phase+'-second')
21527         second = session.stop()
21528         ...
21529     except BaseException as error:
21530         for name in (phase, phase+'-barrier', phase+'-first', phase+'-second'):
21531             state = ledger.state(name)
21532             if state == 'PASSED':
21533                 continue                              # a passed document is final
21534             if state == 'ATTEMPTED':
21535                 # it was EXECUTED and it failed: an explicit FAIL that keeps
21536                 # the raw facts and the barrier facts
21537                 record(name, {'status': 'FAIL', 'executed': True,
21538                               'reason': type(error).__name__,
21539                               'detail': str(error),
21540                               'barrier': dict(api.barrier),
21541                               **raw.get(name, {})})
21542                 ledger.fail(name, type(error).__name__)
21543             # a PLANNED name is left to the outer inventory (NOT_RUN)
21544         raise
21545     finally:
21546         ... # the bounded teardown of the phase (unchanged)
21547 ```
21548 
21549 **The three residual triggers are closed by construction:**
21550 
21551 * **Trigger 1 (executed failure without FAIL):** the failure handler now
21552   rewrites the document of **every attempted** name as `FAIL`, including a
21553   name whose raw document was already written (`raw[name]` keeps the facts).
21554   A name in state `PASSED` is skipped — a passed document is terminal.
21555 * **Trigger 2 (attempted stop ⇒ NOT_RUN):** `ledger.attempt(phase+'-first')`
21556   runs **before** `session.stop()`. If the stop raises, the name is
21557   `ATTEMPTED` → the handler writes **FAIL** (with the exception type and the
21558   live facts), never `NOT_RUN`.
21559 * **Pre-inventory failures:** C12 moves the inventory to the top of the test.
21560 
21561 ### 3.6 C10a — the durable barrier facts **before** the relevant assertions
21562 
21563 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D1).** The `barrier_entered` event and the
21564 > wait "immediately after `session.start()`" of this draft are **wrong** and
21565 > are withdrawn: the barrier of the seam runs only when the coordination of
21566 > the round actually cancels the read, which in this schedule is caused by
21567 > `bind_deadline` / `clock.advance` **after** the worker and the generation
21568 > are registered. §10.2 replaces this subsection with the causal steps S1–S9,
21569 > the `barrier_completed` event and the explicit premise failure on a
21570 > timeout.
21571 
21572 * `_M09TimeoutApi.cancel_synchronous_io` (`T10:3899-3994`) sets a new event
21573   `barrier_entered` **at the top of the barrier block** (before the wait for
21574   the outcome). The event is a *wait*, not an assertion: a phase that waits
21575   for it and then writes the barrier document cannot lose the barrier facts
21576   to an earlier assertion.
21577 * The phase waits for it with a bounded 15 s wait **only** when the barrier
21578   is expected to run (`expect_barrier in ('PASSED','REFUSED')`). For
21579   `NOT_APPLICABLE` (the confirmed coordination) the barrier document is
21580   written immediately with the (empty) barrier snapshot, exactly as today
21581   (`T10:4227-4232`).
21582 * The barrier document is written **before** the assertions at `T10:4192-4232`
21583   — this ordering already exists and is kept.
21584 * The barrier snapshot of the failure path (`T10:4304-4306`) is **kept** — it
21585   is the salvage of the barrier facts into the FAIL record.
21586 
21587 ### 3.7 C11 — `_m09_published_fault_phase` (`T10:4414-4619`)
21588 
21589 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D2, D5).** The construction moves **inside**
21590 > the local guard with `None`-initialised holders, the construction and the
21591 > result join the inventory, and the phase result is written **last** — see
21592 > §10.3 and §10.6.
21593 
21594 The same three rules, with the same call sites:
21595 
21596 * `ledger.attempt(phase + '-construction')` before `_chain(...)`
21597   (`T10:4447-4449`);
21598 * `ledger.attempt(phase)` before `session.start()` (`T10:4467`);
21599 * `ledger.attempt(phase+'-first')` / `attempt(phase+'-second')` before the two
21600   real stops (`T10:4554`, `T10:4564`);
21601 * the failure handler (`T10:4575-4597`) rewrites every **attempted** name as
21602   `FAIL` with the raw facts and the trace; the names that were never entered
21603   stay `PLANNED` for the outer inventory.
21604 
21605 ### 3.8 C12 — the outer inventory of `test_n10_r10` (`T10:4622-4963`)
21606 
21607 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D2).** The inventory grows to the **complete**
21608 > list of §10.3(b) (five names per schedule, 28 in total, including the
21609 > construction and the phase result), and the whole-test guard of §10.3(d)
21610 > covers the earlier R10 real-chain work **and** the coordination block
21611 > **and** the five later schedules.
21612 
21613 **Current:** the inventory (`T10:4904-4912`) and the `try/except` that
21614 installs it (`T10:4913-4963`) are installed **after** the earlier r10 real
21615 checks (`T10:4745-4816`) and after the coordination block (`T10:4817-4888`).
21616 A failure there exits the test before the inventory guard is entered, and the
21617 five later schedule documents stay **absent** — ambiguous, not `NOT_RUN`.
21618 
21619 **Proposed (C12):** the complete document list and the ledger are installed
21620 at the **very top** of the test, before *any* setup and before *any*
21621 assertion, and the **whole** body is inside the guard:
21622 
21623 ```python
21624 def test_n10_r10_the_outcome_of_the_generation_wins_over_the_cancellation(...):
21625     ledger = _PhaseLedger()
21626     r10_documents = []
21627     for r10_name in ('r10-timeout-confirmed', 'r10-timeout-failed',
21628                       'r10-barrier-absent', 'r10-barrier-wrong-generation'):
21629         r10_documents.extend([r10_name, r10_name + '-barrier',
21630                                r10_name + '-first', r10_name + '-second'])
21631     r10_documents.extend(['r10-published-before-timeout',
21632                            'r10-published-before-timeout-first',
21633                            'r10-published-before-timeout-second'])
21634     # EVERY document is named BEFORE anything runs
21635     for r10_name in r10_documents:
21636         ledger.plan(r10_name)
21637     try:
21638         document = _live_plan_document()          # the setup of the test
21639         plan = validate_launch_plan(document, now=time.time())
21640         ...
21641         session.start()                            # the earlier r10 checks
21642         ...
21643         _m09_timeout_phase(..., ledger=ledger)     # the five schedules
21644         ...
21645     except BaseException as error:
21646         raise                                      # the original failure wins
21647     finally:
21648         # every document that was never entered is NOT_RUN; a document that
21649         # was entered and failed was already written as FAIL by its phase
21650         for r10_name in r10_documents:
21651             if ledger.state(r10_name) == 'PLANNED':
21652                 write_phase(r10_name, {'status': 'NOT_RUN',
21653                                        'reason': <the type of the first failure>})
21654 ```
21655 
21656 Properties:
21657 
21658 * The inventory is complete **before** any setup, construction or assertion.
21659 * A document that a phase already wrote is never rewritten by the inventory
21660   (the ledger state is the authority, and the ledger is updated only after a
21661   successful persistence — C9).
21662 * A `NOT_RUN` document carries **no fact** of a phase that was not
21663   established (`write_phase_not_run`, `T10:180-188`, keeps exactly that
21664   shape).
21665 * The `finally` never replaces the original failure: the `except` re-raises
21666   first, and a write failure inside the `finally` is recorded in the receipt
21667   of the test instead of replacing the original exception.
21668 
21669 ### 3.9 C13 — no fabricated facts
21670 
21671 * The `NOT_RUN` document of the outer inventory carries only `status` and
21672   `reason`.
21673 * The `FAIL` document carries the **raw facts that were really observed**
21674   (`raw[name]`), the barrier facts and the exception type/detail — never an
21675   expectation.
21676 * The inventory never writes a `PASSED` document.
21677

21679 
21680 ## 4. M3 — the owner cleanup region, the genuine unwinding, the bounded salvage
21681 
21682 ### 4.1 C14 — the cleanup region encloses `start_round` **and** the RUNNING assertion
21683 
21684 **Current (`T10:3220-3390`):** the inner `try` whose `finally` owns the
21685 cleanup starts at `T10:3233`; `start_round(...)` (`T10:3221-3222`) and the
21686 RUNNING assertion (`T10:3223-3224`) are **outside** it, and the outermost
21687 `finally` (`T10:3388-3389`) releases only the frame. A controlled start
21688 failure or a RUNNING assertion therefore leaves the subcase without the
21689 fixture joins, without the proof and without the captured stop state.
21690 
21691 **Proposed (C14) — the region is moved *outward* (one nesting level):**
21692 
21693 ```python
21694 def controlled_failure(checkpoint):
21695     ...setup (session, registry, gates, holders)...
21696     try:                                     # (A) OUTER: the catch is OUTSIDE
21697         try:                                 # (B) the cleanup region
21698             controlled_start_return = start_round(controlled_session, ...)
21699             # the RUNNING assertion is made on the RETURNED evidence of the
21700             # public start (C3) and it is INSIDE the cleanup region
21701             assert controlled_start_return['state'] == 'RUNNING', ...
21702             ... build the child objects ...
21703             ... the deliberate failure is RAISED here (C15) ...
21704         finally:                             # (C) the cleanup region
21705             gate.set(); controlled_api.frames_ready.set()
21706             ... close the transport and the endpoints (each in its own try) ...
21707             controlled_stop = _capture_stop(controlled_session)   # C20
21708             owners, hints = _registry_owners(...)
21709             salvage = _salvage_threads(owners, states=hints)      # C18
21710             proof = _prove_salvage(salvage, 'the controlled round')
21711             facts = {... 'cleanup_ran_while_unwinding':
21712                         sys.exc_info()[0] is not None, ...}
21713             write_phase('r07-controlled-failure-%s' % checkpoint.lower(), facts)
21714             if proof is not None and sys.exc_info()[0] is None:
21715                 raise AssertionError(proof)
21716     except <the exact expected type> as error:   # (D) caught OUTSIDE (B) and (C)
21717         raised = {'type': type(error).__name__, 'token': str(error)}
21718     return facts
21719 ```
21720 
21721 Properties:
21722 
21723 * `start_round` and the RUNNING assertion are inside the cleanup region: a
21724   failure of either is cleaned up, joined and proved.
21725 * The deliberate exception **propagates through** the cleanup region (C) and
21726   is caught in (D) — **outside** the entire cleanup region. The cleanup
21727   demonstrably runs **while the exception is unwinding**: the region records
21728   `cleanup_ran_while_unwinding = (sys.exc_info()[0] is not None)` inside its
21729   `finally`, which is a **fact**, not an assumption.
21730 * The proof failure of the cleanup never replaces the failure that is already
21731   unwinding (`sys.exc_info()[0] is None` guard, preserved from `T10:3386`).
21732 * The frames/gates are released **unconditionally** in the outer `finally`
21733   (`T10:3388-3389`).
21734 
21735 ### 4.2 C15/C22 — genuine exception-unwind negative tests, exact type and token
21736 
21737 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D4).** The substring test
21738 > `'controlled_close_failure' in detail` is **withdrawn**: the oracle is the
21739 > **exact** class, the **exact** message, exactly one owner and zero
21740 > unrelated failures. §10.4 also states the exact propagation/catch order per
21741 > checkpoint and makes explicit that the `CLOSE_FAILURE` checkpoint is **not**
21742 > an unwinding case (its failure is produced by the cleanup itself).
21743 
21744 The caller (`T10:3392-3413`) asserts the **exact** type and the **exact**
21745 token of the deliberate failure, per checkpoint:
21746 
21747 | checkpoint | deliberate failure | exact type assertion | exact token assertion |
21748 |---|---|---|---|
21749 | `PARENT_ADMISSION` | `raise _R07Sentinel(checkpoint)` inside the region | `type(error) is _R07Sentinel` | `str(error) == 'PARENT_ADMISSION'` |
21750 | `CHILD_TRANSPORT` | `raise _R07Sentinel(checkpoint)` inside the region | `type(error) is _R07Sentinel` | `str(error) == 'CHILD_TRANSPORT'` |
21751 | `ORDINARY_ASSERTION` | `assert controlled_session.state == 'NOT_A_STATE'` inside the region | `type(error) is AssertionError` | the message of the assertion is the group's own message |
21752 | `CONSTRUCTOR_FAILURE` | the seam raises inside the constructor (C16) | `type(error) is _R07ConstructorFailure` | `str(error) == 'CONSTRUCTOR_FAILURE'` |
21753 | `CLOSE_FAILURE` | the close seam raises inside the cleanup | the recorded close failure has `type == 'RuntimeError'` | `'controlled_close_failure' in detail` |
21754 
21755 Every one of these is **raised inside** the cleanup region and **caught
21756 outside** it (C14). The current code catches them **inside** the region
21757 (`T10:3317-3321`, `T10:3323-3326`, `T10:3290-3291`) and therefore only proves
21758 a *normal* `finally` after a caught error — not the cleanup *while
21759 unwinding*.
21760 
21761 **C22 — the close oracle rejects unrelated failures.** The current oracle
21762 (`T10:3411-3413`) only asks whether *some* record has
21763 `owner == 'controlled:transport'`. Proposed (strictly stronger):
21764 
21765 ```
21766 close_failures = controlled_results['CLOSE_FAILURE']['close_failures']
21767 assert len(close_failures) == 1                       # exactly one failure
21768 assert close_failures[0]['owner'] == 'controlled:transport'
21769 assert close_failures[0]['type'] == 'RuntimeError'     # the EXACT type
21770 assert 'controlled_close_failure' in close_failures[0]['detail']   # the EXACT token
21771 # and NO unrelated failure is tolerated:
21772 assert not [f for f in close_failures if f['owner'] != 'controlled:transport']
21773 assert not [f for f in close_failures if f['type'] != 'RuntimeError']
21774 ```
21775 
21776 and, for **every** checkpoint, the ordinary-failure oracle of the *main* child
21777 block (`child_close_failures`, `T10:2929-2964`) is asserted to be **empty**
21778 except for the one intended failure — an unrelated close/endpoint error is a
21779 failure of the test, never a tolerated extra.
21780 
21781 ### 4.3 C16 — the constructor seam: the original `Thread.start` takes effect, **then** raises **inside** the constructor
21782 
21783 **Current (`T10:3273-3291`):** `controlled_failing_channel` calls the whole
21784 real constructor and raises **after** it returned. It therefore tests a lost
21785 assignment after a *successful* construction — not the partial-start trigger.
21786 
21787 **Proposed (C16):** the seam wraps the **original** `threading.Thread.start`
21788 and raises **after** the real start returned, so the thread really takes
21789 effect and the exception is raised **inside** the constructor
21790 (`B:5278`, inside the constructor's `try` at `B:5268-5283`):
21791 
21792 ```python
21793 original_thread_start = threading.Thread.start
21794 
21795 def start_then_raise(thread, *args, **kwargs):
21796     if thread.name != 'lvw-native-custody-channel' or not armed:
21797         return original_thread_start(thread, *args, **kwargs)   # forwarded
21798     registry.mark_starting(thread)                 # immediate registration
21799     original_thread_start(thread, *args, **kwargs) # the thread REALLY starts
21800     registry.mark_started(thread)
21801     raise _R07ConstructorFailure('CONSTRUCTOR_FAILURE')  # inside the constructor
21802 
21803 with unittest.mock.patch.object(threading.Thread, 'start', start_then_raise):
21804     transport = broker_module.StreamChannel(...)     # the constructor raises
21805 ```
21806 
21807 Properties:
21808 
21809 * The **original** start is called and its result is honoured — the thread
21810   really runs; the seam only decides **when** the constructor fails.
21811 * The seam is **round-scoped** by the thread name (`'lvw-native-custody-channel'`,
21812   `B:5257`) and by the `armed` flag: every other thread of the test is
21813   forwarded untouched.
21814 * The patch is installed **only** around the constructor call and is removed
21815   by the context manager (no leak into the rest of the module).
21816 * The **partial channel custody** is preserved: `B:5266-5267` retains the
21817   channel with its custody **before** it builds anything, and the fixture's
21818   `_RegistryCustody` (`T10:257-289`) forwards the original call
21819   (`self._original.retain(kind, resource, detail)` — the original signature
21820   of `B:7436`). The registry therefore holds the partially constructed channel
21821   and the fixture's cleanup can close it and join its drain thread.
21822 * Because the drain thread really started, its start provenance is
21823   `STARTED` (C17) — not `UNKNOWN` — and the cleanup must really end it.
21824 
21825 ### 4.4 C17 — prompt owner registration and the quiescence condition
21826 
21827 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D3).** `pending_starts() == 0` alone is
21828 > **withdrawn** as a proof: a start may still happen after the snapshot.
21829 > §10.5 defines the ownership scope of every round lifetime, the registration
21830 > of the **exact thread object**, the seam that stays armed through the stop
21831 > and the late closer, and the **bounded drain** with **one overall bound**
21832 > (30 s) across the resnapshots — the quiescence assertion comes **after** the
21833 > drain, never before it, and an unproven drain fails truthfully while every
21834 > registered owner is still attempted.
21835 
21836 **Current:** the registry registers **containers** (a session, an endpoint, a
21837 channel) — `T10:2242`, `T10:2336`, `T10:2877-2885`, `T10:3253-3263` — and the
21838 actual threads are discovered **later** from a product that may already have
21839 dropped them (`_session_owners` `T10:415-446`, `_endpoint_owners`
21840 `T10:449-471`, `_channel_owners` `T10:474-496`). There is **no** proof that
21841 every start had returned when the final snapshot is taken.
21842 
21843 **Proposed (C17) — a transparent start-registration seam:**
21844 
21845 * A module-level holder `start_registry = {'value': None}` (the same pattern
21846   as `api_table` / `round_clock` / `round_registry` at `T10:2250`, `T10:2274`,
21847   `T10:2280`).
21848 * The seam wraps `threading.Thread.start` and forwards the original start.
21849   It registers the thread **immediately before** the original start (state
21850   `STARTING`) and marks it `STARTED` right after the original start returned
21851   (state `STARTED`); if the original start raises, the state is `FAILED` and
21852   the error is kept.
21853 * Only the **named** production threads of this package are registered, so
21854   the seam is transparent for everything else:
21855   `'lvw-native-custody-channel'` (`B:5257`), `'lvw-native-custody-pipe-read'`
21856   / `'lvw-native-custody-pipe-write'` (`B:4680`),
21857   `'lvw-native-custody-channel-pump'` (`C:791`),
21858   `'lvw-native-custody-heartbeat'` (`C:1390`),
21859   `'lvw-native-custody-closer'` (`C:1531`).
21860 * The registry gains three small methods: `mark_starting(thread)`,
21861   `mark_started(thread)`, `pending_starts()`.
21862 
21863 **Quiescence condition (asserted before the final snapshot):**
21864 
21865 ```
21866 assert registry.pending_starts() == 0, \
21867     'a start of the round had not returned when the owners were enumerated'
21868 ```
21869 
21870 The final owner snapshot is taken **only after** the quiescence condition
21871 holds; a non-zero pending count is a failure of the cleanup proof (the owner
21872 is `UNKNOWN`), never a silent omission.
21873 
21874 ### 4.5 C18 — the salvage attempts **ALL** owners, even when a join or a liveness query fails
21875 
21876 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D5).** The **classification** of the owner
21877 > (`_owner_start_state`) moves **inside** the per-owner guard, and every
21878 > error is retained as a **list** with its kind, its exact type and its
21879 > detail — never a single "first error" and never a silent `UNKNOWN` without
21880 > a diagnostic. §10.7 gives the final shape and the
21881 > `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit` rule.
21882 
21883 **Current (`T10:326-360`):** only `RuntimeError` from `join` is caught; **any
21884 other** exception from `join`, and **any** exception from `is_alive()`,
21885 aborts the iteration — the remaining owners are never joined and the proof
21886 document is never written.
21887 
21888 **Proposed (C18):**
21889 
21890 ```python
21891 def _salvage_threads(owners, *, seconds=10.0, states=None, total_seconds=30.0):
21892     facts = []
21893     hints = states or {}
21894     deadline = time.monotonic() + total_seconds
21895     for name, thread in owners:
21896         state = _owner_start_state(thread, hints.get(name))
21897         if state != 'STARTED':
21898             facts.append({'name': name, 'start_state': state,
21899                           'started': None if state == 'UNKNOWN' else False,
21900                           'alive': None, 'joined': None, 'error': None})
21901             continue
21902         error = None; alive = None; joined = False
21903         try:
21904             wait = max(0.0, min(seconds, deadline - time.monotonic()))
21905             thread.join(wait)
21906         except BaseException as exc:                 # ANY failure of the join
21907             error = {'type': type(exc).__name__, 'detail': str(exc)}
21908         try:
21909             alive = bool(thread.is_alive())
21910             joined = not alive
21911         except BaseException as exc:                 # ANY failure of the query
21912             error = error or {'type': type(exc).__name__, 'detail': str(exc)}
21913             alive = None; joined = False
21914         facts.append({'name': name, 'start_state': state, 'started': True,
21915                       'alive': alive, 'joined': joined, 'error': error})
21916     return facts
21917 ```
21918 
21919 Properties:
21920 
21921 * **Every** owner is attempted — a failing `join` or a failing `is_alive` is
21922   recorded and the iteration continues.
21923 * The failure is **retained**, not swallowed: it is in the facts of the owner
21924   and it **fails the proof** (`_prove_salvage` must return a failure for an
21925   owner with `alive is None` or `error is not None`).
21926 * The cleanup is **bounded**: at most `seconds` (10 s) per owner and at most
21927   `total_seconds` (30 s) for the whole salvage; the wait of an owner is
21928   cropped by the remaining total.
21929 * The salvage is **separate** from the product: it renews no deadline of the
21930   round, it erases no retained resource and it never claims that the product
21931   released anything (the docstring of `T10:326-339` is kept).
21932 
21933 ### 4.6 C19 — the start state needs **proven provenance**
21934 
21935 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D5).** The classification rule itself stands;
21936 > a **failure** of the classification is now handled inside the per-owner
21937 > guard and is recorded with its diagnostic (§10.7).
21938 
21939 **Current (`T10:292-323`):** an owner without an identity that is not alive
21940 is mapped to `NEVER_STARTED` (`T10:323`) — a guess, not a proof.
21941 
21942 **Proposed (C19):**
21943 
21944 ```python
21945 def _owner_start_state(thread, hint=None):
21946     if thread is None:
21947         return 'NEVER_STARTED'
21948     ident = getattr(thread, 'ident', None)      # guarded by try/except
21949     if ident is not None:
21950         return 'STARTED'
21951     if hint in ('STARTED', 'NEVER_STARTED', 'UNKNOWN'):
21952         return hint                              # proven provenance (C17)
21953     return 'UNKNOWN'                             # no provenance => UNKNOWN
21954 ```
21955 
21956 `NEVER_STARTED` is now returned **only** when the registry proves that the
21957 start was never invoked (or when the thread object does not exist at all).
21958 An ident-less owner without provenance is `UNKNOWN` and **fails the proof**.
21959 
21960 ### 4.7 C20 — the stop: the exception **plus** the live state and the retention, before the salvage
21961 
21962 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D5, root factual correction).** The capture
21963 > names the **real** keys of the evidence DTO — including
21964 > `background_threads`, which is a valid key (`C:2399-2406`) — and keeps the
21965 > **object identities** (`session.broker is …`, `id(session.broker)`) apart
21966 > from the display JSON. A snapshot that fails records an explicit
21967 > `snapshot_error`; no key is invented and no valid key is read with a
21968 > `.get()` that could hide an absent value.
21969 
21970 **Current (`T10:396-412`):** on an exception the capture keeps only the type
21971 and the detail; the live state and the retained resources of the moment are
21972 lost.
21973 
21974 **Proposed (C20):**
21975 
21976 ```python
21977 def _capture_stop(session):
21978     captured = {'returned': None, 'exception': None, 'live_state': None,
21979                 'retained': None, 'retained_broker_id': None,
21980                 'background_threads': None}
21981     if session is None:
21982         return captured
21983     try:
21984         captured['returned'] = session.stop()
21985     except BaseException as error:
21986         captured['exception'] = {'type': type(error).__name__,
21987                                  'detail': str(error)}
21988         # the live state and the retention are read NOW, before the salvage
21989         try:
21990             captured['live_state'] = session.state
21991             captured['retained'] = session.broker is not None
21992             captured['retained_broker_id'] = id(session.broker)
21993             captured['background_threads'] = session.evidence().get(
21994                 'background_threads')
21995         except BaseException:                     # the facts stay visible
21996             captured['live_state'] = 'UNKNOWN'
21997     else:
21998         captured['retained'] = session.broker is not None
21999         captured['retained_broker_id'] = id(session.broker)
22000     return captured
22001 ```
22002 
22003 The stop exception is never discarded, and the live state / retention of the
22004 moment are recorded **before** the salvage of the fixture.
22005 
22006 ### 4.8 C21 — the reversed fallback arguments
22007 
22008 **Current (`T10:537-541`):**
22009 
22010 ```python
22011 if session is not None and 'session' not in kinds:
22012     add(_session_owners('%s:session' % prefix, session, hints))   # reversed
22013 if channel is not None and 'channel' not in kinds:
22014     add(_channel_owners('%s:channel' % prefix, channel, hints))   # reversed
22015 ```
22016 
22017 `_session_owners(session, prefix='session', hints=None)` and
22018 `_channel_owners(channel, prefix, hints)` take the **object first**; the
22019 fallback passes the **name string** as the object and the object as the
22020 prefix. The dedup key (`id(thread)`) is then computed over a string.
22021 
22022 **Proposed (C21):**
22023 
22024 ```python
22025 if session is not None and 'session' not in kinds:
22026     add(_session_owners(session, '%s:session' % prefix, hints))
22027 if channel is not None and 'channel' not in kinds:
22028     add(_channel_owners(channel, '%s:channel' % prefix, hints))
22029 ```
22030 
22031 (the registry-loop calls at `T10:529-534` are already in the correct order and
22032 are unchanged).
22033 
22034 ### 4.9 The deadline of the product is preserved
22035 
22036 Every wait of the fixture is the **fixture's** own bounded wait (≤ 10 s per
22037 owner, ≤ 30 s per salvage, ≤ 15 s per observation, ≤ 30 s per gate). None of
22038 them renews, extends or publishes a deadline of the round; the product's own
22039 cleanup deadline (`C:2121-2133`) and the original `STOP_CLEANUP_SECONDS`
22040 budget are untouched. The salvage is the work of the **test** and it is
22041 recorded separately from the returned state of the product.

The exact controlled-failure predicate is **restored** in a stronger form. |

22176 ## 10. Correction addendum — root review D1–D5 (authoritative)
22177 
22178 Revises the design after the root review (`CHANGES_REQUIRED`, D1–D5). It
22179 **supersedes** §3.5–§3.8, §4.2, §4.4–§4.7 and the rows C10, C11, C12, C14,
22180 C15, C17–C20, C22 of §6. Everything else stands (C1–C9, C13, C16, C21, §2,
22181 §5, §7–§9). No framework is added: the causal order, the exception boundaries,
22182 the inventory and the transitions of the named items are fixed.
22183 
22184 ### 10.1 (D1) — the barrier: the wait may not precede its cause
22185 
22186 **Withdrawn:** the `barrier_entered` event and the wait "right after
22187 `session.start()`" of §3.6 — the barrier of the seam runs only when the
22188 coordination cancels the read, which `bind_deadline` + `clock.advance`
22189 (`T10:4139-4140`) cause **after** the worker and the generation are
22190 registered (`T10:4125-4134`). The original trigger is preserved, never moved:
22191 
22192 | step | action | where |
22193 |---|---|---|
22194 | S1 | `session.start()` | `T10:4119` |
22195 | S2 | bounded wait 15 s for `api.read_waiting` | `T10:4123` |
22196 | S3 | `worker = holder['read_endpoint']._reader`; `api.worker_holder['worker'] = worker` | `T10:4125-4127` |
22197 | S4 | `generation = worker._submitted`; `api.worker_holder['generation'] = generation` | `T10:4128-4134` |
22198 | S5 | `bind_deadline(clock.value + 0.5)`; `clock.advance(1.0)` → the coordination cancels the read → the seam's `cancel_synchronous_io` runs | `T10:4139-4140` |
22199 | S6 | **in the seam**: publish the fault → the barrier block → the predicates → `barrier['left_at']` → **the seam persists `api.barrier_snapshot = dict(self.barrier)`** → **the seam sets `api.barrier_completed`** | seam `T10:3899-3994` |
22200 | S7 | the phase waits (bounded 15 s) for `api.barrier_completed` | new |
22201 | S8 | the phase writes the durable barrier document **from the persisted snapshot** | new |
22202 | S9 | the barrier assertions read the **persisted snapshot** | `T10:4192-4232` |
22203 
22204 * The event is **`barrier_completed`**, set by the seam at the **end** of the
22205   barrier block; no "entered" event, no wait before S5.
22206 * The snapshot is written **by the seam**; the phase never re-reads the live
22207   `api.barrier`, so a late snapshot can never look completed.
22208 * A **timeout** of S7 persists an explicit premise failure —
22209   `{'status': 'FAIL', 'premise': 'BARRIER_NOT_COMPLETED', 'timeout_seconds':
22210   15.0, 'barrier_completed': False}` — and the phase fails; it never
22211   continues with an empty barrier.
22212 * `expect_barrier='NOT_APPLICABLE'`: the barrier never runs, the document is
22213   written **immediately** with the empty snapshot and
22214   `barrier_snapshot['entered_at'] is None` is asserted (`T10:4227-4232`); no
22215   wait is performed there.
22216 * The failure path keeps the barrier facts (`T10:4304-4306`) and adds
22217   `barrier_completed` and the snapshot when it exists.
22218 
22219 ### 10.2 (D2) — the construction, the phase result, the whole-test guard
22220 
22221 **(a) The construction is inside the local guard**, with the holders
22222 initialised to `None` before it: `ledger.attempt(phase + '-construction')`,
22223 then `session = holder = channel_closes = channel_facts = None`, then `try:`
22224 → `_chain(api, document, plan, tmp_path, clock=clock)` → the phase body →
22225 `except BaseException:` (the FAIL rewrite of §10.6) → `raise` → `finally:`
22226 (the bounded teardown; a `None` holder is skipped, never dereferenced). A
22227 construction that failed half way is therefore an **attempted construction**
22228 with a durable FAIL document, not an absent document.
22229 
22230 **(b) The complete inventory** — five names per schedule: `<phase>` (the
22231 **result**), `<phase>-construction`, `<phase>-barrier`, `<phase>-first`,
22232 `<phase>-second`; plus `r10-published-before-timeout{,-first,-second}` and
22233 the earlier R10 documents `r10-first`, `r10-second`, `r10-coordination` →
22234 **31 names**, all `plan`ned at the top of the test.
22235 
22236 **(c) The result is separate from the checks.** A passed check is terminal.
22237 The result document is written **last**, after both stops **and** the cleanup,
22238 and becomes PASSED only when the barrier check is PASSED (or NOT_APPLICABLE),
22239 both stop checks are PASSED and the cleanup had no proof failure. A later
22240 failed stop ⇒ the result is **FAIL** while the earlier checks **keep** PASSED
22241 and their facts. The result is never PASSED before the stops and the cleanup.
22242 
22243 **(d) The whole-test guard** covers the earlier R10 real-chain work
22244 (`T10:4745-4816`), the coordination block (`T10:4817-4888`) **and** the five
22245 later schedules; the inventory and the ledger are installed before all of it;
22246 the `finally` writes `NOT_RUN` only for the names still PLANNED and never
22247 overwrites a written document.
22248 
22249 ### 10.3 (D3) — the scope, the exact thread objects, the bounded drain
22250 
22251 **(a) The scope** — one registry per round lifetime; the seam is armed for
22252 the whole lifetime and disarmed only after that round's salvage: the R07 main
22253 round (`parent_registry`, armed before `start_round(...)` at `T10:2371`,
22254 disarmed after the parent salvage at `T10:2983-2995`); the zero round
22255 (`zero_registry`, `T10:2682` → `T10:2786-2789`); each controlled subcase
22256 (`controlled_registry`, `T10:3221` → `T10:3370-3374`). The seam stays armed
22257 through the product's `stop()` and the late closer work, so a thread started
22258 during the stop is registered too.
22259 
22260 **(b) The exact object, not the name** — the registration is keyed by
22261 `id(thread)`; the name is only a label. The seam forwards every start it
22262 does not own (`if id(thread) not in armed_threads and thread.name not in
22263 owned_names: return original_start(thread, *args, **kwargs)`); the ownership
22264 proof always works on the object, and a name match alone never claims
22265 ownership.
22266 
22267 **(c) No production decision is frozen** — the seam observes only: it
22268 forwards the original start, never blocks, refuses, reorders or delays a
22269 start, and never touches a deadline.
22270 
22271 **(d) The bounded drain, ONE overall bound** — `pending_starts() == 0` alone
22272 is withdrawn as a proof (a start may follow the snapshot). The salvage of a
22273 round is a bounded drain loop: `budget = 30.0` (one overall bound per
22274 round), `deadline = now + budget`; then repeatedly — take `registry.snapshot()`
22275 (the exact objects and their states) and append it to `attempts`; release the
22276 gates of the round; `_salvage_threads(snapshot.owners, states=snapshot.hints,
22277 seconds=10.0, total_seconds=max(0.0, deadline - now))`; stop when
22278 `quiescent` (no pending start, no late start) **and** the salvage is proved,
22279 or when `now >= deadline`. The last snapshot and the last salvage are the
22280 recorded facts.
22281 
22282 * The **30 s** is the bound of the **whole drain of that round**, not 30 s per
22283   resnapshot; the per-owner wait is cropped by the remaining overall budget
22284   and the budget is **never reset** between the rounds of the loop nor between
22285   the rounds of the test.
22286 * The quiescence assertion comes **after** the drain, never before it: an
22287   unquiet round is a **FAIL/UNKNOWN** — the gates are still released and
22288   **all** the registered owners are still attempted; the drain repeats
22289   boundedly; if the bound is reached the proof fails truthfully (`'the owners
22290   of the round were not quiescent'`) with the last snapshot and the last
22291   salvage recorded.
22292 * The drain never renews a deadline of the product and never claims that the
22293   product released a resource.
22294 
22295 **(e) The producers** are the ones the product starts: pump and heartbeat
22296 (`C:1772-1783`), closer (`C:1530-1534`), channel drain (`B:5256-5278`), the
22297 two endpoint workers (`B:4683-4702`) — all observed, because the seam
22298 observes every `threading.Thread.start` of the armed window.
22299 
22300 ### 10.4 (D4) — the exact close failure, the exact unwinding order
22301 
22302 **(a) The substring test is withdrawn.** The oracle is exact: exactly one
22303 recorded failure; `owner == 'controlled:transport'`; `type == 'RuntimeError'`
22304 (the exact class); `detail == 'controlled_close_failure'` (the exact
22305 message); and no record with another owner or another type. In **every**
22306 checkpoint `child_close_failures` (`T10:2929-2964`) must be **empty**: an
22307 unrelated close or endpoint error fails the subcase instead of being
22308 tolerated next to the intended failure.
22309 
22310 **(b) The exact ordering** for the four checkpoints whose deliberate failure
22311 is raised by the fixture: (1) the deliberate failure is **raised** inside the
22312 region (sentinel / ordinary assertion / constructor seam); (2) the region
22313 runs **every** cleanup action in a fixed order — the gates → the close of the
22314 transport → the close of each endpoint → `_capture_stop` → the owner
22315 enumeration → the drain + salvage → the proof → the document; (3) the region
22316 **records** every additional error and raises `AssertionError(proof)` **only**
22317 when no original failure is unwinding; (4) the original failure leaves the
22318 region and is caught by the outer `except`, **after every other cleanup
22319 action has been attempted**; (5) the outer `except` records the exact type
22320 and the exact token.
22321 
22322 `CLOSE_FAILURE` is the single case whose failure is produced **by the
22323 cleanup itself**: the failing close is **recorded** with its exact type and
22324 exact message and the region **continues** with every other cleanup action —
22325 it is therefore **not** an unwinding case, and the design says so instead of
22326 claiming it. No expected sentinel is caught before the cleanup region: the
22327 outer `except` is the only catch and it lies outside the region.
22328 
22329 **(c) The original failure is preserved** — an error met by the region while
22330 an original failure unwinds leaves the **original** re-raised, the additional
22331 error recorded in the document and the overall proof failed; the test never
22332 reports a successful cleanup on an error.
22333 
22334 ### 10.5 (D5) — every cleanup error is preserved
22335 
22336 **(a) The classification is inside the per-owner guard** (it was outside the
22337 try of the salvage in §4.5). Per owner: `state = None; errors = []`; then
22338 `_owner_start_state(...)` inside its own `try` (a failure ⇒ an `errors`
22339 entry of kind `STATE` and `state = 'UNKNOWN'`); if the state is not
22340 `STARTED` the owner is recorded with `alive=None, joined=None` and its
22341 errors; otherwise `thread.join(wait)` in its own `try` (kind `JOIN`) and
22342 `bool(thread.is_alive())` in its own `try` (kind `LIVENESS`, `alive = None`
22343 on a failure); the fact of the owner keeps `alive`, `joined` and the **list**
22344 `errors`.
22345 
22346 * **every** owner is attempted — a failure of the classification, of the join
22347   or of the liveness query never aborts the iteration;
22348 * every error is retained in a **list** with its kind, exact type and detail
22349   — never a single "first error", never a silent `UNKNOWN` without a
22350   diagnostic; an owner whose classification failed is `UNKNOWN` **with** the
22351   diagnostic and it fails the proof, which names the owner and the error;
22352 * the display form (the thread name) and the identity (`id(thread)`) are
22353   separate fields — the identity is never read out of a display string.
22354 
22355 **(b) `KeyboardInterrupt` / `SystemExit`** — the interruption is recorded
22356 with its identity; with no original unwinding it is re-raised at the end of
22357 the region; with an original unwinding the **original** is preserved and
22358 re-raised and the interruption is an additional recorded error. The region
22359 never reports a successful cleanup when an interruption occurred.
22360 
22361 **(c) `_capture_stop` reads the real facts** — the **real** keys of the
22362 evidence DTO (`C:2343-2444`), among them `background_threads`, which **is** a
22363 valid key (`C:2399-2406`); the object identities are kept apart from the
22364 display JSON. The capture holds: `returned` (the actual dict of
22365 `session.stop()`), `exception` (`{'type','detail'}`), `live_state`
22366 (`session.state`), `evidence` (the full dict of `session.evidence()`),
22367 `evidence_state`, `evidence_broker_retained`, `evidence_failures`,
22368 `evidence_background_threads`, `evidence_closer_start_state` (the real keys
22369 of that dict), `retained_broker_is_session_broker` (a bool: the identity),
22370 `retained_broker_id` (`id(session.broker)`: the identity) and `snapshot_error`
22371 (`{'type','detail'}` when the snapshot failed).
22372 
22373 * the identities are **not** read out of the display JSON — they are the live
22374   facts of the session; the display JSON is kept as the DTO it is;
22375 * a valid key is never read through a `.get()` that could hide an absent
22376   value — a missing value is a fact to be asserted;
22377 * if the snapshot raises, `snapshot_error` carries the exact type and detail
22378   and the capture is **not** silently empty;
22379 * the capture is taken **before** the salvage and on **both** paths.
22380 
22381 ### 10.6 (D2, D6) — the state transitions after the corrections
22382 
22383 | from | event | to | durable document |
22384 |---|---|---|---|
22385 | `PLANNED` | the operation is entered (`attempt()` **before** the construction, the phase body, the barrier or the stop) | `ATTEMPTED` | none yet |
22386 | `PLANNED` | the end of the test, never entered | `NOT_RUN` | `{'status': 'NOT_RUN', 'reason': <type of the first failure>}` — no fact of the phase |
22387 | `ATTEMPTED` | the raw facts are written, before the assertions | `ATTEMPTED` | `{'status': 'EXECUTED', ...raw facts...}` |
22388 | `ATTEMPTED` | every check of the operation held | `PASSED` | the **check** document — terminal |
22389 | `ATTEMPTED` | an assertion raised or the operation itself raised | `FAIL` | the check document: `{'status': 'FAIL', 'executed': True, 'reason': <type>, 'detail': <str>, ...raw facts...}` |
22390 | `ATTEMPTED` | the phase reached its end | `PASSED` / `FAIL` | the **result** document, written **last**; PASSED only when the barrier check, both stop checks **and** the cleanup passed; a later failed stop ⇒ FAIL while the earlier checks keep PASSED |
22391 | `PASSED` / `FAIL` / `NOT_RUN` | anything | unchanged (**terminal**) | never overwritten by the inventory |
22392 
22393 The **result** and the **check** documents are different: the result carries
22394 the overall outcome, the checks carry their own facts; a failed check never
22395 rewrites a passed check and the inventory never rewrites either.

00239   888         """Wait for one reply of the wanted kinds, bounded by the deadline.
00240   889 
00241   890         The **original** context of the round is read **again** at the
00242   891         moment of the wait: a deadline that was published after the
00243   892         caller built its number shortens this wait.  A number that was
00244   893         constructed earlier is never the authority of a wait.
00245   894         """

00247   896         with self._lock:
00248   897             for index, reply in enumerate(self._pending):
00249   898                 if reply['kind'] in kinds:
00250   899                     del self._pending[index]
00251   900                     return reply
00252   901             if 'STATUS' in kinds and self._latest_status is not None:
00253   902                 reply = self._latest_status
00254   903                 self._latest_status = None
00255   904                 return reply
00256   905             if self._error is not None:
00257   906                 raise self._error
00258   907             if self._eof:
00259   908                 raise CustodyError('CUSTODY_CHANNEL_EOF')
00260   909             self._waiters.append(waiter)

00262   911         context = self._context
00263   912         if context is not None:
00264   913             current = context.effective_deadline()
00265   914             if current is not None:
00266   915                 limit = current if limit is None else min(limit, current)
00267   916         remaining = limit - self._clock()

00270   919                 if waiter in self._waiters:
00271   920                     self._waiters.remove(waiter)
00272   921             raise CustodyError('CUSTODY_CHANNEL_TIMEOUT')
00273   922         if waiter.reply is not None:
00274   923             return waiter.reply
00275   924         with self._lock:
00276   925             failure = self._error
00277   926         if failure is not None:
00278   927             raise failure

### /mnt/c/workspace/videoworkline/localviewworkbench/LVW_Prompt_Service_MasterPack_v2.0.0/.agent-governance/README.md
00001 # LVW Agent Governance
00002 
00003 版本：1.0.0（2026-10-27）
00004 
00005 本目录把多项目、多 Agent 协作规则接入现有 MasterPack。它只管理“谁可以做什么、候选如何绑定、证据如何生成、Stage 如何裁决”，不复制或改写产品权威。
00006 
00007 ## 权威顺序
00008 
00009 1. 用户当前明确授权。
00010 2. `docs/00_POSITION_AND_ADR.md` 与批准的 ADR。
00011 3. `contracts/`、`plans/requirements.json`、`plans/acceptance_cases.json`、`plans/release_gates.json`。
00012 4. 当前冻结的 `.agent-governance/stages/<stage-id>/`。
00013 5. 本目录的通用治理规则与模板。
00014 6. `legacy/`，只读历史。
00015 
00016 冲突不得静默覆盖。公共合同、固定分母、阈值或角色权限变化必须新建变更记录，由门禁负责人裁决并重新冻结 Stage Packet。
00017 
00018 ## 文件关系
00019 
00020 - `roles.md`：角色、权限和四权分离。
00021 - `routing-policy.md`：任务路由、预算和升级。
00022 - `stage-gates.md`：Stage、Workpack、候选和门禁状态机。
00023 - `parallel-execution.md`：跨项目队列、worktree 与资源隔离。
00024 - `anti-false-green.md`：生产路径、证据和反假绿规则。
00025 - `workflows/`：阶段生命周期的可测试工作流规范。
00026 - `templates/`：可复用交接、收据、审查和裁决模板。
00027 - `stages/V0-S0/`：首个真实 Stage Packet；当前只冻结流程，未执行目标机验收。
00028 - `runtime/`：可变队列、收据和指标的接口说明；实际运行数据默认不提交源码仓库。
00029 - `project-registry.json`：跨项目调度的项目入口；这里只登记LVW，不扫描或接管其他项目。
00030 - `plans/execution-control.json`：唯一当前坐标。
00031 - `tools/verify_governance.py`：确定性制度校验和反假绿负例自测。
00032 
00033 ## 固定状态边界
00034 
00035 产品用例继续只使用 `NOT_RUN/PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED`。执行调度使用 `DRAFT/READY/RUNNING/READY_FOR_REVIEW/CHANGES_REQUIRED/VERIFIED`。Stage 裁决使用 `PASS/NO_GO/BLOCKED/WAIT_BUDGET/WAIT_AUTH`。三类状态不得互相冒充。
00036 
00037 ## 最小闭环
00038 
00039 ```text
00040 冻结 Stage Packet
00041 -> 派生 Workpack
00042 -> 隔离实现
00043 -> 实现收据
00044 -> 受控自动验收
00045 -> 隔离独立复算
00046 -> Codex 门禁裁决
00047 -> 必要的人类签署
00048 ```
00049 
00050 运行：
00051 
00052 ```bash
00053 python3 tools/verify_governance.py
00054 python3 tools/verify_governance.py --self-test
00055 ```
00056 
00057 两条命令只验证制度结构和负例拒绝能力，不是 LVW 产品验收。

### /mnt/c/workspace/videoworkline/localviewworkbench/LVW_Prompt_Service_MasterPack_v2.0.0/docs/24_EXECUTION_MASTER_PLAN.md
00001 # 24｜开发执行总纲：V0 完整收口与 V1–V3 扩展
00002 
00003 修订日期：2026-11-06。性质：现有范围的执行文档整理；不激活新 Stage、不批准发布、不修改冻结合同或门限。
00004 
00005 ## 入口、权威与完成度
00006 
00007 无命令启动入口：根目录 `启动LVW.lnk` / `LVW.exe`，说明见[启动器](../launcher/README.md)。该辅助启动增量不修改当前Stage分母或替代人工签署。
00008 
00009 验收报告与新视频入口：[逐项报告、原测试视频与11段未跑LVW的留样](../验收报告与盲测视频.html)。新样本预期已冻结，只辅助人工判断，不替代S3质量集或改变Stage分母。
00010 
00011 人工体验与记录入口：[根目录人工验收指南](../人工验收指南.html)，启动及验收说明见[docs/26](26_MANUAL_ACCEPTANCE_GUIDE.md)。该辅助页不改固定分母、不代签。
00012 
00013 先读 `plans/execution-control.json`，再读本章、当前 Stage Packet 和对应实现章节。产品需求、用例、发布门禁分别以 `plans/requirements.json`、`plans/acceptance_cases.json`、`plans/release_gates.json` 为准。实现设计见 docs/13–20；历史范围决策见 docs/22–23。`plans/tasks.json` 是依赖/范围目录，其中初始 NOT_RUN 不是实时进度；实时进度只保存在 execution-control 的 development_outline，与证据路径绑定。
00014 
00015 本章是执行索引，不复制第二套合同或当前坐标。下表是2026-11-06审计快照；后续每次停止时从 execution-control 重列大纲并标出当前 Stage。文末过往运行更新保留历史，不再作为待授权或待执行指令。当前 S2 已到人工门槛，机器/独审通过不等于人工签署。
00016 
00017 完成度使用“已完成子项/列明子项”，不把不同复杂度子项换算为工时百分比。分别报告实现、机器验收、独立审查、人工签署；文件存在、测试数量和旧候选通过都不能替代当前产品验收。未审计代码不能武断标为未实现；应写“未完成正式交付/验收，需复用审计”。

00036 
00037 ## V0 范围、输入输出与非目标
00038 
00039 V0-Min 提供单图→本地模型→raw/建议→显式采纳→人工四输出→复制/TXT/JSON；V0.1 增加最简短视频、文件边界与资源/取消；V0.2 补离线、增量安装/回滚、质量验证。V0 无持久任务数据库，Comfy 不可用时不保证界面可用；独立 React 服务是 R1a/V1 路线。
00040 
00041 图片 JPEG/PNG/WebP，≤20 MiB/40 MP，长边≤1024；视频 MP4/MOV，≤256 MiB/60s，源单帧≤8294400 像素，默认四帧、送模型长边≤768。短片只有 1–3 个不同时间点可少帧并警告，不复制同帧。8 帧高级配置未验证，不开放。原媒体不变，记录源 hash、尺寸、实际采样时间性质和局限。精确长片分镜、ASR、训练、下载模型、任意网络输入、资产库、V2/V3 对端集成均不是 V0 交付要求。
00042 
00043 四输出为自然中英、图像 Prompt、视频 Prompt、标签，负向可空。静图运动属于创作补充，不当成观测；英文缺失明确展示，CPU 格式化不能伪装翻译。用户稿与 raw/建议分离，分析失败、拒答、重试、取消和晚到均不得自动覆盖人工内容。不增设 NSFW 审核/审批，不承诺本地模型永不拒答。
00044 
00045 ## V0 全部需求覆盖与执行责任
00046 
00047 下表覆盖全部 V0-R01–R12 / V0-A01–A12。每项必须有生产入口、驱动、Oracle、负例、持久终态/原始证据和清理。正式阈值仍由当前合同与冻结 packet 决定；此表不是降低或扩展分母的授权。
00048 
00049 | 需求/用例 | Stage / 生产 owner | 测试与明确 Oracle | 失败/清理与交付 |
00050 |---|---|---|---|
00051 | R01 / A01 图片真实输入 | S1；ControlledImageOwner → LVWImagePromptBridge → 本机 Ollama | 原 hash 不变；EXIF/透明/像素限额；公开工作流真模型返回 raw/建议；S2 累计回归 | 超限/损坏不启动推理；错误保留人工稿；image UI/API 图与来源元数据 |
00052 | R02 / A02 视频有限抽帧 | S2；video_input/decoder/process → LVWVideoPromptOwner | 静态/跟拍/快切/VFR；实际顺序、PTS/time base/hash 可复算；受控解码，真 Provider 调用 | 0/5 帧、重复/倒退时间、短片少帧有明确终态；自有解码子进程/快照清理；video UI/API 图 |
00053 | R03 / A03 四输出合同 | S1，S2 累计；core/manual 与原生 JS | 相同建议切换/导出不新增视觉调用；Schema 与落盘 JSON/TXT 回读一致 | 状态/卸载日志可追加，但原日志前缀与 chat 计数必须校验；不能接受日志改写 |
00054 | R04 / A04 人工编辑导出 | S1，S2 累计；ManualDraftOwner | 无模型时 20,000 字编辑、复制、原子导出；不依赖 GPU 分支 | 导出失败保留稿/旧目标，无临时残留；人工 workflow/独立面板 |
00055 | R05 / A05 异常不覆盖 | S1，S2 累计；state/run token/draft_epoch | 无效 JSON、拒答、超时、OOM、过期回调不得写稿；显式采纳 | 真实故障与合成负例分别标记；raw 保留且脱敏；无自动无限重试 |
00056 | R06 / A06 断网增量迁移 | S3；打包/install/diagnose/rollback owner（待冻结） | 中文/空格隔离路径安装；断网冷启动；无非 loopback 外联尝试；回滚后旧工作流实际可用 | 部分安装、冲突、篡改 fail-closed；只动隔离根，不复制权重、不写永久配置 |
00057 | R07 / A07 文件安全 | S2；video_files/upload/允许根 | 公共入口测 traversal、绝对/UNC、reparse、损坏/伪扩展、超大小/时长、提示注入 | 拒绝发生于 Provider 前；不能越界写入或清理，不执行媒体元数据内容 |
00058 | R08 / A08 无审批前置 | S1，S2 累计；人工公开入口 | 空稿、无模型、任意普通内容备注均能编辑/导出合法 manual 结果 | 无内容审核节点/云回退/审批状态前置；不能把供应商拒答改写为成功 |
00059 | R09 / A09 资源与性能 | S2；runtime/sampler/warm phase | 默认冷加载另报；热图10+热四帧10；nearest-rank P95≤180/300s；GPU<23552 MiB，RAM≥2048 MiB，OOM=0 | 已批准改为共享模型空闲/预测预算（当前required_free=19047MiB），运行峰值硬限不变；竞争停止不抢占；每秒采样含确定进程集合；热测试结束回默认卸载 |
00060 | R10 / A10 取消卸载 | S2；request/resource owner → 公开取消 → native audit | 准备/推理取消；反馈≤1s；当前 packet 自取消起≤30s 物理释放；晚到不发布、不改稿 | 关闭 HTTP 不是停 GPU；/api/ps 空与显存回基线+1024 连续3次；仅本轮 PID/birth 可清理；不误杀 |
00061 | R11 / A11 图片质量 | S3；独立预标注与评分 owner | 冻结10图，原始结果五维各0–2，≥8且无关键幻觉；至少8/10可用 | 未答/缺失占失败，不替换样本，不以人工改稿/模型自评通过 |
00062 | R12 / A12 视频质量 | S3；独立预标注与评分 owner | 冻结6片，动作/运镜/局限；至少5/6可用，无关键幻觉 | 四类结构样本不能替代6片质量集；逐片原始证据与释放；不能拼接正例 |
00063

00084 
00085 初次文档修订时的历史准备状态（现已被full08结果取代）：当时补充授权请求的完整范围已获用户批准，但该文档批次仅登记批准，不发 ACTIVE 子授权，不探测 GPU、不读媒体、不启动服务/浏览器。计划审阅后的继续指令才解除 hold；同一范围无需再次请求重复批准。若采用下一章会改变候选权限/测试预算的提案，先记录变更及其与原授权的差异，不能把旧批准静默扩展。

00094 | S3-P2 安装/回滚 | 同一实现 owner 连续完成 | 受控隔离根 install/diagnose/rollback，原文件 hash、操作账本、恢复点与卸载说明 | 冲突/部分写入/篡改/越界/回滚失败负例；失败不破坏旧环境；不修改现有永久配置；当前母授权范围不足时单列变更 |
00095 | S3-P3 独立质量集与评分准备 | 独立标注 owner；实现者只提供执行器 | 非私有10图+6片、来源/授权/样本hash、五维rubric和预标注、不可用计分规则 | 先冻结标注再模型执行；样本不能因失败替换；已有体验审计只作选材/风险参考，不能冒充独立正式质量 |
00096 | S3-P4 离线集中收口 | CI | 包结构、合同、安装负例、导出/回滚、V0累计回归；候选绑定收据 | 每个批次先定向；Stage结束一次完整离线检查，失败集中纠偏，不每改一文件全回归 |
00097 | S3-P5 真实累计验收 | 受控 CI | 新子授权；离线冷启、中文/空格目录迁移、回滚、原工作流、质量16个样本、十二项总账 | 原始逐次结果、环境/资源、外联尝试观测、完整清理；现行母授权最多一次完整checkpoint+一次修正完整复验，额度不足停止 |
00098 | S3-P6 独审/人工/交付 | reviewer → gate owner → 人类 | 重算12项、独立质量、无权重增量包、使用/卸载/回滚入口、候选/签署/完整文件清单 | Fatal/Major=0；人类仅作体验/质量/风险判断；签署后立即推送；缺质量仍是 QUALITY_PENDING，不声称V0.2或V1通过 |
00099 
00100 安装/回滚命令与构建脚本目前尚无该目录的成套产物，不能给出假称可执行的命令。S3-P1/P2 交付命令、help、参数合同及测试；进入 Gate0 前填明准确入口和隔离根规则。详见 `reports/v0-s3/preparation-01.md`，它只保存历史准备，不是当前进度源。
00101 
00102 ## 测试、证据、成本和恢复的共同要求
00103 
00104 实现内循环只运行变更 owner 的定向测试/合同负例；Stage集中验收再运行相关子树。仓库现有离线工具为 `tools/v0_s2_offline_checkpoint.py`，真实协调器为 `tools/v0_s2_stage_checkpoint.py`；二者不混用，不能在当前 hold 期间执行后者。本轮文档校验仅使用 verify_pack/verify_governance 和引用/分母交叉检查，不重新跑模型或461项产品测试。
00105 
00106 每批实现收据保留改动、合同变化或none、命令/退出码、生产路径和风险。正式运行必须绑定 candidate/spec/acceptance_hash/gate/run/environment、样本、实际工具/model digest、原始日志及产物 SHA、明确分母、失败/未执行、资源与清理。模型文字说明只作导航，旧失败不改写。
00107 
00108 新候选使受影响证据失效；现行完整真实候选不允许跨运行拼接或旧输出替换。只在既有冻结复用规则明确允许时复用不受影响证据。恢复先读唯一坐标与原终态，禁止因会话断开重启仍在执行的原运行，禁止对 lease.closed=1 的 slot 重放。未知进程/目录保留并报告，不强制杀删。
00109 
00110 现有 V1 母授权与补充授权的界限继续有效：仅本机 loopback、非私有固定媒体、无云/付费/下载/可见浏览器/永久配置/误杀；每轮子授权和原始事实来自受控执行器。预算/权限/合同/独审边界触发即停；人工签署与最终发布不能代签。
00111 
00112 ## V1–V3 如何少量扩展此计划
00113 
00114 沿用需求ID、owner、输入输出合同、工作批次、定向检查、集中验收、独审与签署八个栏目，不复制另一套系统。V1 扩展 docs/14 的服务/事务/任务细节；V2 扩展 docs/15 的PTS、资产、MCP和恢复；V3 扩展 docs/16 的真实对端合同与授权。各 Stage 只补实际文件允许范围、冻结样本/预算和准确命令；运行前实际依赖未满足仍不得省略 Gate0。
00115 
00116 后续计划已有产品和合同基础，但没有逐 Stage 冻结过的执行包，不能称“文档已保证无人值守完成全部版本”。特别是 V3 的对端真实 API/权限、V2 新依赖和 V1 便携宿主必须到阶段前核实；这些属于有名有主的进入条件，不靠大量重写全项目 PRD 解决。
00117

00084 ## 2. M1 — the public zero-admission chain (test module only)

00086 ### 2.1 C1 — the malformed patch (the review's trigger 1)
00087 
00088 **Current (T10:2676-2677):**
00089 
00090 ```python
00091 with unittest.mock.patch.object(broker_module, 'BrokerProcess',
00092                                 'read', zero_gated_broker_read), \
00093      unittest.mock.patch.object(custody_module, '_ReplyWaiter',
00094                                 ZeroTighteningWaiter):
00095 ```
00096 
00097 `unittest.mock.patch.object(target, attribute, new, spec, ...)` — the third
00098 positional argument is **`new`**, not a spec. The call therefore assigns the
00099 **string** `'read'` to the *module* attribute `BrokerProcess`; the real class
00100 is never patched, `B:7896` then tries to call that string, the launcher
00101 failure is swallowed by `C:1744-1756` and the round returns a structured
00102 failure — so **no** attached pump and **no** public reply admission is ever
00103 created for the zero round. This is a static control/data-flow conclusion; no
00104 runtime failure is claimed here.
00105 
00106 **Proposed (C1):** patch the **class method** with the class as the target:
00107 
00108 ```python
00109 with unittest.mock.patch.object(broker_module.BrokerProcess, 'read',
00110                                 zero_gated_broker_read), \
00111      unittest.mock.patch.object(custody_module, '_ReplyWaiter',
00112                                 ZeroTighteningWaiter):
00113 ```
00114 
00115 * `zero_gated_broker_read(self, timeout)` (`T10:2610-2624`) keeps the
00116   **original signature** of `BrokerProcess.read` (`B:6467-6468`:
00117   `def read(self, timeout): return self._channel.read(timeout)`), so the
00118   replacement is a plain function installed on the class and it is called as
00119   `broker.read(timeout)` → `zero_gated_broker_read(broker, timeout)`.
00120 * The replacement **forwards** the original unbound method
00121   (`zero_original_broker_read = broker_module.BrokerProcess.read`, captured
00122   at `T10:2590` **before** the patch) → `zero_original_broker_read(self, timeout)`.
00123   The original result is returned unchanged.
00124 * The gate is **round-scoped**: it only holds the broker whose
00125   `self._context is zero_session._context`; every other broker keeps the
00126   original behaviour (`T10:2618-2619`).
00127 * The `_ReplyWaiter` patch is unchanged: `custody_module._ReplyWaiter`
00128   (`C:764`) is looked up at **call time** inside `_ChannelPump.take`
00129   (`C:895`), so the patch really intercepts the waiter that the **public**
00130   start builds (`C:1784`, `C:1793`).
00131 
00132 **Scope / max wait / negative oracle:** the patch lives only inside the
00133 zero-round `with` block (`T10:2675-2685`) and is removed by the context
00134 manager. The gate wait is bounded by `ZERO_GATE_SECONDS = 30.0`
00135 (`T10:145`); the admission wait is bounded by `ZERO_ADMISSION_SECONDS = 15.0`
00136 (`T10:146`). Negative oracle: if the gate is never reached, `zero_gate_facts`
00137 is empty → `C7`/`Z10` fails with *"the admission of the zero round never
00138 reached the gate"*; if the gate timed out, `zero_gate_facts[0]['released'] is
00139 False` → *"the gate of the admission of the zero round timed out"*.
