00141 ### 2.2 C2 — the actual error value vs. its display `repr`
00142 
00143 **Current:** `T10:2650-2651` stores `repr(pump.error)` into
00144 `zero_premise['pump_error_at_admission']` and `T10:2705-2706` stores
00145 `repr(zero_pump.error)` into the facts; `T10:2733` then requires that stored
00146 value to `is None`. A healthy pump has `error is None`, so `repr(None)` is the
00147 **string** `'None'` and the premise can never hold.
00148 
00149 **Proposed (C2):** keep the *display* form for the human-readable document but
00150 store the **actual** value separately, and assert on the actual value:
00151 
00152 | key | value | use |
00153 |---|---|---|
00154 | `pump_error_is_none` | `pump.error is None` (a real `bool`) | the assertion oracle |
00155 | `pump_error_type` | `type(pump.error).__name__` or `None` | the failure name |
00156 | `pump_error_repr` | `repr(pump.error)` or `None` | the display form only, **never** an oracle |
00157 
00158 `T10:2733` becomes
00159 `assert zero_premise['pump_error_is_none'] is True` (plus
00160 `assert zero_premise['pump_error_repr'] is None` as the redundant display
00161 check). The same split is applied to the facts document at `T10:2705-2706`
00162 (`zero_pump_error_is_none`, `zero_pump_error_type`, `zero_pump_error_repr`).
00163 
00164 ### 2.3 C3/C4 — the **actual** public start return
00165 
00166 `NativeCustodySession.start()` (`C:1709-1818`) **returns** `self.evidence()`
00167 (`C:1808`, `C:1750`, `C:1754`, `C:1780`, `C:1798`) and never raises for an
00168 ordinary failure. The fixture's `start_round` (`T10:2314-2352`) calls
00169 `round_session.start()` at `T10:2347` and **discards** the return, returning
00170 the session object instead (`T10:2352`); `T10:2689` then re-reads
00171 `zero_session.evidence()` — a *later* evidence object, not the one the public
00172 operation returned.
00173 
00174 **Proposed (C3):** `start_round` keeps its arguments and captures the public
00175 return value:
00176 
00177 ```python
00178 start_return = round_session.start()      # the ACTUAL return of the public start
00179 ...
00180 return start_return                        # the return of the helper
00181 ```
00182 
00183 All three call sites bind it:
00184 
00185 * `T10:2371` → `parent_start_return = start_round(session, api, clock, parent_registry)`
00186 * `T10:2682` → `zero_start_return = start_round(zero_session, zero_api, zero_clock, zero_registry)`
00187 * `T10:3221` → `controlled_start_return = start_round(controlled_session, controlled_api, controlled_clock, controlled_registry)`
00188 
00189 (The helper returns the start result instead of the session; the session
00190 object itself is already in scope at every call site, so no other use is
00191 lost.)
00192 
00193 **Proposed (C4):** the zero round uses the **captured return** as the returned
00194 state of the product — `zero_returned = zero_start_return` — and the later
00195 `zero_session.evidence()` is used only as a **cross-check** that the state
00196 did not change after the return (`zero_session.evidence()['state'] ==
00197 zero_start_return['state']`). The original failure is never overwritten by the
00198 later read.

00200 ### 2.4 C5 — the actual public start / retention oracle
00201 
00202 `evidence()` always supplies the key `broker_retained` (`C:2361`), so a
00203 key-presence check (`T10:2772`) proves nothing. The **value** of the
00204 retention and the **identity** of the retained resource are the oracle.
00205 
00206 | id | oracle (exact predicate) | fact source | failure message |
00207 |---|---|---|---|
00208 | **Z1** | `zero_start_return['state'] == 'UNKNOWN_RETAINED'` | the value returned by the public `start` | *the public start of the zero round did not latch its state* |
00209 | **Z2** | `'CUSTODY_CHANNEL_TIMEOUT' in zero_start_return['failures']` | same return (`C:1812-1813`) | *the public start of the zero round did not name the timeout of the admission* |
00210 | **Z3** | `'CUSTODY_CHANNEL_EOF' not in zero_start_return['failures']` | same return | *the round ended at the end of the stream instead of the timeout* |
00211 | **Z4** | `zero_start_return['broker_retained'] is True` | same return (`C:2361`) | *the round did not retain its broker* |
00212 | **Z5** | `zero_broker is not None and zero_session.broker is zero_broker` | the live attribute (`C:991`, `C:1741`) and the object of the round | *the retained original resource is not the object of the round* |
00213 | **Z6** | `zero_start_return['broker']['identity_source'] == 'PARENT_ORIGINAL_HANDLE'` **and** `zero_start_return['broker']['pid'] == zero_broker.pid` | same return (`C:1755-1761`) | *the identity of the broker is a claim and not the original handle* |
00214 | **Z7** | `zero_start_return['pump_error'] is None` | same return (`C:2365-2367`) | *the pump of the round failed before the admission* |
00215 | **Z8** | `zero_pump is zero_session._pump` **and** `zero_pump._context is zero_session._context` **and** `zero_pump.finished is True` | the **attached** pump (`C:1772`, `C:1782`) | *the attached pump of the zero round is not the pump of the session / did not end / has another context* |
00216 | **Z9** | `zero_queue_waits[-1] == 0.0` **and** `zero_reply_waits[-1] == 0.0` | the **actual arguments** the production passed (`T10:2604`, `T10:2663`) | *the round asked for a wait after the expiry* |

00219 | **Z12** | `_assert_salvage_proved(zero_salvage, 'the round of zero')` | the salvage facts | *an owner of the zero round was left behind* |
00220 
00221 Z1–Z3 are the **exact cause** of the failure (the timeout, not the EOF, not a
00222 launcher refusal); Z4–Z6 are the **actual retention** (value + identity of
00223 the retained original resource); Z8–Z10 are the **bounded, checked**
00224 no-EOF / timeout facts; Z11 is the ordering; Z12 is the bounded cleanup.

00226 ### 2.5 C6/C7 — the actual ordering, with the bounded checked no-EOF/timeouts
00227 
00228 A single ordered trace is recorded during the zero round. Every event is
00229 appended **at the moment it happens**, by the transparent seam, with its
00230 actual argument:
00231 
00232 | id | event | recorded at | recorded argument |
00233 |---|---|---|---|
00234 | **E1** | `START_CALLED` | `start_round`, immediately **before** `round_session.start()` | — |
00235 | **E2** | `PUMP_READ_ENTERED` | `zero_gated_broker_read`, before the gate wait (`T10:2620`) | the `timeout` the production passed |
00236 | **E3** | `REPLY_WAIT_ENTERED` | `ZeroTighteningWaiter.recording_wait`, before the original wait (`T10:2664`) | the `timeout` the production passed |
00237 | **E4** | `REPLY_WAIT_RETURNED` | immediately **after** the original wait returned and **before** `zero_gate.set()` (`T10:2665-2670`) | the original result (`False` at the zero expiry) |

00240 | **E7** | `PUMP_ENDED` | the observation loop (`T10:2696-2700`) | `zero_pump.finished` |

00242 **Required order (the assertion of Z11):**
00243 `E1 < E2 < E3 < E4 < E5 < E6 < E7`.
00244 
00245 * `E2 < E3` — the waiter of the reply is built by the admission of the public
00246   start (`C:895`) and its constructor waits for `zero_held`
00247   (`T10:2644-2645`), which is set inside the held read (`T10:2620`).
00248 * `E4 < E5` — the gate is released by the reply waiter **after** the reply
00249   wait returned (`T10:2666-2670`); the pump is therefore still held while the
00250   reply admission completes, and the end of the stream / the error of the
00251   pump can never preempt the reply the round owes.
00252 * `E5 < E6` — the attached pump performs its real read of the channel
00253   (`B:5496-5529`) only after the gate was released.
00254 * `E6 < E7` — the pump really ends.

00261 | **N2** | the failure cause is the **timeout** and not the EOF (Z2 + Z3) — the round really failed on the admission, not on an early end of stream | `C:1874-1890` (the code of the failure) | — |
00262 | **N3** | every queue wait recorded **after** `E5` has `timeout == 0.0` — a round whose bound arrived asks for nothing (`B:5513-5520`) | `T10:2604-2606` | ≤ the recorded arguments |

00268 ### 2.6 Exception boundaries of the zero block (M1)
00269 
00270 The zero block keeps **one** `try/finally` whose `finally` owns the salvage
00271 (`T10:2775-2796`), and the boundary is explicit:
00272 
00273 * **Inside** the `try`: the public start, the observation of the attached
00274   pump, the durable document `r07-zero-public-chain` and the assertions Z1–Z11.
00275 * **Inside** the `finally`: `zero_gate.set()` and `zero_api.frames_ready.set()`
00276   (the gates are released **unconditionally**), then `_capture_stop`,
00277   `_registry_owners`, `_salvage_threads`, `_prove_salvage`, the durable
00278   document `r07-zero-salvage`, and the raising of the proof failure **only**
00279   when no other failure is unwinding (`sys.exc_info()[0] is None`).
00280 * **Never** inside: a `try/except` that swallows the failure of the public
00281   start. The public start returns a structured failure instead of raising
00282   (`C:1744-1756`, `C:1806-1817`) — the design therefore asserts on the
00283   **returned** value, and it does not convert a refusal into a skip.

00287 ## 3. M2 — truthful phase inventory, FAIL vs NOT_RUN, durable barrier
00288 
00289 ### 3.1 C8 — the attempt ledger (one small local helper)
00290 
00291 A module-level ledger, used by the two M09 phase helpers and by the outer
00292 `test_n10_r10` test:
00293 
00294 ```
00295 _PHASE_STATES = ('PLANNED', 'ATTEMPTED', 'PASSED', 'FAIL', 'NOT_RUN')
00296 
00297 class _PhaseLedger:
00298     def plan(self, name):        # named before it runs
00299     def attempt(self, name):     # AT THE MOMENT the operation is entered
00300     def pass_(self, name):       # only after every assertion of it held
00301     def fail(self, name, reason):# it was attempted and it failed
00302     def state(self, name):       # PLANNED / ATTEMPTED / PASSED / FAIL
00303     def names(self):             # in the frozen order
00304 ```
00305 
00306 The ledger is **not** a framework: it is one small class next to
00307 `_OwnerRegistry` (`T10:214-254`) with the same shape (a lock + a list) and
00308 the same purpose (remembering, never deciding).
00309 
00310 ### 3.2 State-transition table
00311 
00312 | from | event | to | durable document |
00313 |---|---|---|---|
00314 | `PLANNED` | the operation is **entered** (`attempt()` — called *before* the construction, the phase body or the stop call) | `ATTEMPTED` | none yet |
00315 | `PLANNED` | the end of the test, the operation was never entered | `NOT_RUN` | `{'status': 'NOT_RUN', 'reason': <type of the first failure>}` — **no facts of the phase** |
00316 | `ATTEMPTED` | the raw facts are written (durable, before the assertions) | `ATTEMPTED` (unchanged) | `{'status': 'EXECUTED', ...raw facts...}` |
00317 | `ATTEMPTED` | every assertion of the operation held | `PASSED` | rewrite of the same path: `{'status': 'PASSED', ...raw facts...}` |
00318 | `ATTEMPTED` | an assertion raised **or** the operation itself raised | `FAIL` | rewrite of the same path: `{'status': 'FAIL', 'executed': True, 'reason': <type>, 'detail': <str>, ...raw facts...}` |
00319 | `PASSED` / `FAIL` / `NOT_RUN` | anything | unchanged (**terminal**) | never overwritten by the inventory |
00320 
00321 ### 3.3 Document lifecycle table
00322 
00323 | document | written when | final status written by |
00324 |---|---|---|
00325 | `<phase>-barrier` | **before** the first assertion that depends on the barrier | the phase (PASSED) or the failure handler (FAIL) |
00326 | `<phase>` | the raw facts, **before** the assertions | the phase (PASSED) or the failure handler (FAIL) |
00327 | `<phase>-first` / `<phase>-second` | right after the corresponding **actual** stop returned | the phase (PASSED) or the failure handler (FAIL) — an **attempted** stop that raises is FAIL, never NOT_RUN |
00328 
00329 `write_phase` (`T10:149-155`) overwrites the file at the same path, so the
00330 "raw facts" write and the "final status" write are the **same** document:
00331 the final status never erases the raw facts, it adds the verdict.
00332 
00333 ### 3.4 C9 — a document is marked *written* only **after** persistence succeeded
00334 
00335 **Current (`T10:4104-4116` and `T10:4458-4463`):**
00336 
00337 ```python
00338 def record(name, facts):
00339     written.add(name)                 # marked BEFORE the write
00340     if inventory is not None:
00341         inventory.add(name)            # marked BEFORE the write
00342     return write_phase(name, facts)
00343 ```
00344 
00345 A `write_phase` that raises (disk error, encoding error) leaves the name
00346 marked as written although no document exists.
00347 
00348 **Proposed (C9):**
00349 
00350 ```python
00351 def record(name, facts):
00352     path = write_phase(name, facts)    # the persistence FIRST
00353     written.add(name)                  # marked only after it succeeded
00354     if inventory is not None:
00355         inventory.add(name)
00356     ledger.pass_or_fail(name, ...)     # the ledger follows the same rule
00357     return path
00358 ```
00359 
00360 The `written` set and the inventory are then a **reliable** membership test
00361 for "a document exists on disk".
00362 
00363 ### 3.5 C10 — `_m09_timeout_phase` (`T10:4032-4329`)
00364 
00365 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D1, D2, D5, D6).** The shape below is
00366 > superseded by §10.2 (the causal order of the barrier), §10.3 (the
00367 > construction inside the local guard, the phase result document and the
00368 > whole-test guard) and §10.6 (the transitions). The pseudocode below is kept
00369 > only as the shape of the helper; **the ordering of the barrier wait and the
00370 > inventory/result rules of §10 are authoritative**.
00371 
00372 Proposed shape (pseudocode; the production is untouched):
00373 
00374 ```python
00375 def _m09_timeout_phase(document, plan, tmp_path, *, phase, confirm_the_worker,
00376                         hold_the_worker, barrier_probe='EXACT',
00377                         expect_barrier='PASSED', inventory=None, ledger=None):
00378     ledger.plan(phase); ledger.plan(phase+'-barrier')
00379     ledger.plan(phase+'-first'); ledger.plan(phase+'-second')
00380     api = _M09TimeoutApi(confirm_the_worker=confirm_the_worker,
00381                          hold_the_worker=hold_the_worker)
00382     api.barrier_probe = barrier_probe
00383     ledger.attempt(phase + '-construction')          # BEFORE the construction
00384     session, holder, channel_closes, channel_facts = _chain(
00385         api, document, plan, tmp_path, clock=clock)
00386     worker = None
00387     raw = {}                                          # the raw facts per document
00388     try:
00389         ledger.attempt(phase)
00390         session.start()
00391         # -- a WAIT, not an assertion: the barrier announces itself ----
00392         if expect_barrier in ('PASSED', 'REFUSED'):
00393             api.barrier_entered.wait(15.0)             # bounded wait
00394         barrier = dict(api.barrier)                   # the ACTUAL facts
00395         raw[phase + '-barrier'] = {...}                # the facts of the barrier
00396         record(phase + '-barrier', {'status': 'EXECUTED', 'barrier': barrier,
00397                                      'barrier_expectation': expect_barrier, ...})
00398         # -- only NOW the assertions of the phase ------------------------
00399         assert api.read_waiting.wait(15.0), ...
00400         ...
00401         record(phase, {'status': 'EXECUTED', **raw[phase]})
00402         assert <the assertions of the phase>
00403         ledger.pass_(phase)
00404         record(phase, {'status': 'PASSED', **raw[phase]})     # the rewrite
00405         # -- the FIRST real stop ----------------------------------------
00406         ledger.attempt(phase + '-first')
00407         first = session.stop()                        # a raise here => FAIL
00408         raw[phase+'-first'] = {...}
00409         record(phase+'-first', {'status': 'EXECUTED', **raw[phase+'-first']})
00410         assert first_facts.get('channel_reader_error') == 'RuntimeError', ...
00411         assert first['broker_retained'] is True
00412         assert first['state'] == 'UNKNOWN_RETAINED'
00413         ledger.pass_(phase+'-first')
00414         record(phase+'-first', {'status': 'PASSED', **raw[phase+'-first']})
00415         # -- the SECOND real stop ---------------------------------------
00416         ledger.attempt(phase+'-second')
00417         second = session.stop()
00418         ...
00419     except BaseException as error:
00420         for name in (phase, phase+'-barrier', phase+'-first', phase+'-second'):
00421             state = ledger.state(name)
00422             if state == 'PASSED':
00423                 continue                              # a passed document is final
00424             if state == 'ATTEMPTED':
00425                 # it was EXECUTED and it failed: an explicit FAIL that keeps
00426                 # the raw facts and the barrier facts
00427                 record(name, {'status': 'FAIL', 'executed': True,
00428                               'reason': type(error).__name__,
00429                               'detail': str(error),
00430                               'barrier': dict(api.barrier),
00431                               **raw.get(name, {})})
00432                 ledger.fail(name, type(error).__name__)
00433             # a PLANNED name is left to the outer inventory (NOT_RUN)
00434         raise
00435     finally:
00436         ... # the bounded teardown of the phase (unchanged)
00437 ```
00438 
00439 **The three residual triggers are closed by construction:**
00440 
00441 * **Trigger 1 (executed failure without FAIL):** the failure handler now
00442   rewrites the document of **every attempted** name as `FAIL`, including a
00443   name whose raw document was already written (`raw[name]` keeps the facts).
00444   A name in state `PASSED` is skipped — a passed document is terminal.
00445 * **Trigger 2 (attempted stop ⇒ NOT_RUN):** `ledger.attempt(phase+'-first')`
00446   runs **before** `session.stop()`. If the stop raises, the name is
00447   `ATTEMPTED` → the handler writes **FAIL** (with the exception type and the
00448   live facts), never `NOT_RUN`.
00449 * **Pre-inventory failures:** C12 moves the inventory to the top of the test.
00450 
00451 ### 3.6 C10a — the durable barrier facts **before** the relevant assertions
00452 
00453 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D1).** The `barrier_entered` event and the

00475   is the salvage of the barrier facts into the FAIL record.

00495 ### 3.8 C12 — the outer inventory of `test_n10_r10` (`T10:4622-4963`)

00560

00570 ## 4. M3 — the owner cleanup region, the genuine unwinding, the bounded salvage
00571 
00572 ### 4.1 C14 — the cleanup region encloses `start_round` **and** the RUNNING assertion
00573 
00574 **Current (`T10:3220-3390`):** the inner `try` whose `finally` owns the
00575 cleanup starts at `T10:3233`; `start_round(...)` (`T10:3221-3222`) and the
00576 RUNNING assertion (`T10:3223-3224`) are **outside** it, and the outermost
00577 `finally` (`T10:3388-3389`) releases only the frame. A controlled start
00578 failure or a RUNNING assertion therefore leaves the subcase without the
00579 fixture joins, without the proof and without the captured stop state.
00580 
00581 **Proposed (C14) — the region is moved *outward* (one nesting level):**
00582 
00583 ```python
00584 def controlled_failure(checkpoint):
00585     ...setup (session, registry, gates, holders)...
00586     try:                                     # (A) OUTER: the catch is OUTSIDE
00587         try:                                 # (B) the cleanup region
00588             controlled_start_return = start_round(controlled_session, ...)
00589             # the RUNNING assertion is made on the RETURNED evidence of the
00590             # public start (C3) and it is INSIDE the cleanup region
00591             assert controlled_start_return['state'] == 'RUNNING', ...
00592             ... build the child objects ...
00593             ... the deliberate failure is RAISED here (C15) ...
00594         finally:                             # (C) the cleanup region
00595             gate.set(); controlled_api.frames_ready.set()
00596             ... close the transport and the endpoints (each in its own try) ...
00597             controlled_stop = _capture_stop(controlled_session)   # C20
00598             owners, hints = _registry_owners(...)
00599             salvage = _salvage_threads(owners, states=hints)      # C18
00600             proof = _prove_salvage(salvage, 'the controlled round')
00601             facts = {... 'cleanup_ran_while_unwinding':
00602                         sys.exc_info()[0] is not None, ...}
00603             write_phase('r07-controlled-failure-%s' % checkpoint.lower(), facts)
00604             if proof is not None and sys.exc_info()[0] is None:
00605                 raise AssertionError(proof)
00606     except <the exact expected type> as error:   # (D) caught OUTSIDE (B) and (C)
00607         raised = {'type': type(error).__name__, 'token': str(error)}
00608     return facts
00609 ```
00610 
00611 Properties:
00612 
00613 * `start_round` and the RUNNING assertion are inside the cleanup region: a
00614   failure of either is cleaned up, joined and proved.
00615 * The deliberate exception **propagates through** the cleanup region (C) and
00616   is caught in (D) — **outside** the entire cleanup region. The cleanup
00617   demonstrably runs **while the exception is unwinding**: the region records
00618   `cleanup_ran_while_unwinding = (sys.exc_info()[0] is not None)` inside its
00619   `finally`, which is a **fact**, not an assumption.
00620 * The proof failure of the cleanup never replaces the failure that is already
00621   unwinding (`sys.exc_info()[0] is None` guard, preserved from `T10:3386`).
00622 * The frames/gates are released **unconditionally** in the outer `finally`
00623   (`T10:3388-3389`).
00624 
00625 ### 4.2 C15/C22 — genuine exception-unwind negative tests, exact type and token
00626 
00627 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D4).** The substring test
00628 > `'controlled_close_failure' in detail` is **withdrawn**: the oracle is the
00629 > **exact** class, the **exact** message, exactly one owner and zero
00630 > unrelated failures. §10.4 also states the exact propagation/catch order per
00631 > checkpoint and makes explicit that the `CLOSE_FAILURE` checkpoint is **not**

00634 The caller (`T10:3392-3413`) asserts the **exact** type and the **exact**

00636 
00637 | checkpoint | deliberate failure | exact type assertion | exact token assertion |
00638 |---|---|---|---|

00640 | `CHILD_TRANSPORT` | `raise _R07Sentinel(checkpoint)` inside the region | `type(error) is _R07Sentinel` | `str(error) == 'CHILD_TRANSPORT'` |
00641 | `ORDINARY_ASSERTION` | `assert controlled_session.state == 'NOT_A_STATE'` inside the region | `type(error) is AssertionError` | the message of the assertion is the group's own message |
00642 | `CONSTRUCTOR_FAILURE` | the seam raises inside the constructor (C16) | `type(error) is _R07ConstructorFailure` | `str(error) == 'CONSTRUCTOR_FAILURE'` |

00644 
00645 Every one of these is **raised inside** the cleanup region and **caught

00648 a *normal* `finally` after a caught error — not the cleanup *while

00651 **C22 — the close oracle rejects unrelated failures.** The current oracle
00652 (`T10:3411-3413`) only asks whether *some* record has
00653 `owner == 'controlled:transport'`. Proposed (strictly stronger):

00656 close_failures = controlled_results['CLOSE_FAILURE']['close_failures']
00657 assert len(close_failures) == 1                       # exactly one failure
00658 assert close_failures[0]['owner'] == 'controlled:transport'
00659 assert close_failures[0]['type'] == 'RuntimeError'     # the EXACT type
00660 assert 'controlled_close_failure' in close_failures[0]['detail']   # the EXACT token
00661 # and NO unrelated failure is tolerated:
00662 assert not [f for f in close_failures if f['owner'] != 'controlled:transport']
00663 assert not [f for f in close_failures if f['type'] != 'RuntimeError']

00666 and, for **every** checkpoint, the ordinary-failure oracle of the *main* child

00671 ### 4.3 C16 — the constructor seam: the original `Thread.start` takes effect, **then** raises **inside** the constructor
00672 
00673 **Current (`T10:3273-3291`):** `controlled_failing_channel` calls the whole
00674 real constructor and raises **after** it returned. It therefore tests a lost
00675 assignment after a *successful* construction — not the partial-start trigger.
00676 
00677 **Proposed (C16):** the seam wraps the **original** `threading.Thread.start`
00678 and raises **after** the real start returned, so the thread really takes
00679 effect and the exception is raised **inside** the constructor
00680 (`B:5278`, inside the constructor's `try` at `B:5268-5283`):
00681 
00682 ```python
00683 original_thread_start = threading.Thread.start
00684 
00685 def start_then_raise(thread, *args, **kwargs):
00686     if thread.name != 'lvw-native-custody-channel' or not armed:
00687         return original_thread_start(thread, *args, **kwargs)   # forwarded
00688     registry.mark_starting(thread)                 # immediate registration
00689     original_thread_start(thread, *args, **kwargs) # the thread REALLY starts
00690     registry.mark_started(thread)
00691     raise _R07ConstructorFailure('CONSTRUCTOR_FAILURE')  # inside the constructor
00692 
00693 with unittest.mock.patch.object(threading.Thread, 'start', start_then_raise):
00694     transport = broker_module.StreamChannel(...)     # the constructor raises
00695 ```
00696 
00697 Properties:
00698 
00699 * The **original** start is called and its result is honoured — the thread
00700   really runs; the seam only decides **when** the constructor fails.
00701 * The seam is **round-scoped** by the thread name (`'lvw-native-custody-channel'`,
00702   `B:5257`) and by the `armed` flag: every other thread of the test is
00703   forwarded untouched.
00704 * The patch is installed **only** around the constructor call and is removed
00705   by the context manager (no leak into the rest of the module).
00706 * The **partial channel custody** is preserved: `B:5266-5267` retains the
00707   channel with its custody **before** it builds anything, and the fixture's
00708   `_RegistryCustody` (`T10:257-289`) forwards the original call
00709   (`self._original.retain(kind, resource, detail)` — the original signature
00710   of `B:7436`). The registry therefore holds the partially constructed channel
00711   and the fixture's cleanup can close it and join its drain thread.
00712 * Because the drain thread really started, its start provenance is
00713   `STARTED` (C17) — not `UNKNOWN` — and the cleanup must really end it.

00715 ### 4.4 C17 — prompt owner registration and the quiescence condition
00716 
00717 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D3).** `pending_starts() == 0` alone is
00718 > **withdrawn** as a proof: a start may still happen after the snapshot.
00719 > §10.5 defines the ownership scope of every round lifetime, the registration
00720 > of the **exact thread object**, the seam that stays armed through the stop
00721 > and the late closer, and the **bounded drain** with **one overall bound**
00722 > (30 s) across the resnapshots — the quiescence assertion comes **after** the
00723 > drain, never before it, and an unproven drain fails truthfully while every
00724 > registered owner is still attempted.
00725 
00726 **Current:** the registry registers **containers** (a session, an endpoint, a
00727 channel) — `T10:2242`, `T10:2336`, `T10:2877-2885`, `T10:3253-3263` — and the
00728 actual threads are discovered **later** from a product that may already have
00729 dropped them (`_session_owners` `T10:415-446`, `_endpoint_owners`
00730 `T10:449-471`, `_channel_owners` `T10:474-496`). There is **no** proof that
00731 every start had returned when the final snapshot is taken.
00732 
00733 **Proposed (C17) — a transparent start-registration seam:**
00734 
00735 * A module-level holder `start_registry = {'value': None}` (the same pattern
00736   as `api_table` / `round_clock` / `round_registry` at `T10:2250`, `T10:2274`,
00737   `T10:2280`).
00738 * The seam wraps `threading.Thread.start` and forwards the original start.
00739   It registers the thread **immediately before** the original start (state
00740   `STARTING`) and marks it `STARTED` right after the original start returned
00741   (state `STARTED`); if the original start raises, the state is `FAILED` and
00742   the error is kept.
00743 * Only the **named** production threads of this package are registered, so
00744   the seam is transparent for everything else:
00745   `'lvw-native-custody-channel'` (`B:5257`), `'lvw-native-custody-pipe-read'`
00746   / `'lvw-native-custody-pipe-write'` (`B:4680`),
00747   `'lvw-native-custody-channel-pump'` (`C:791`),
00748   `'lvw-native-custody-heartbeat'` (`C:1390`),
00749   `'lvw-native-custody-closer'` (`C:1531`).
00750 * The registry gains three small methods: `mark_starting(thread)`,
00751   `mark_started(thread)`, `pending_starts()`.
00752 
00753 **Quiescence condition (asserted before the final snapshot):**
00754 
00755 ```
00756 assert registry.pending_starts() == 0, \
00757     'a start of the round had not returned when the owners were enumerated'
00758 ```
00759 
00760 The final owner snapshot is taken **only after** the quiescence condition
00761 holds; a non-zero pending count is a failure of the cleanup proof (the owner
00762 is `UNKNOWN`), never a silent omission.
00763 
00764 ### 4.5 C18 — the salvage attempts **ALL** owners, even when a join or a liveness query fails
00765 
00766 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D5).** The **classification** of the owner
00767 > (`_owner_start_state`) moves **inside** the per-owner guard, and every
00768 > error is retained as a **list** with its kind, its exact type and its
00769 > detail — never a single "first error" and never a silent `UNKNOWN` without
00770 > a diagnostic. §10.7 gives the final shape and the
00771 > `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit` rule.
00772 
00773 **Current (`T10:326-360`):** only `RuntimeError` from `join` is caught; **any
00774 other** exception from `join`, and **any** exception from `is_alive()`,
00775 aborts the iteration — the remaining owners are never joined and the proof
00776 document is never written.
00777 
00778 **Proposed (C18):**
00779 
00780 ```python
00781 def _salvage_threads(owners, *, seconds=10.0, states=None, total_seconds=30.0):
00782     facts = []
00783     hints = states or {}
00784     deadline = time.monotonic() + total_seconds
00785     for name, thread in owners:
00786         state = _owner_start_state(thread, hints.get(name))
00787         if state != 'STARTED':
00788             facts.append({'name': name, 'start_state': state,
00789                           'started': None if state == 'UNKNOWN' else False,
00790                           'alive': None, 'joined': None, 'error': None})
00791             continue
00792         error = None; alive = None; joined = False
00793         try:
00794             wait = max(0.0, min(seconds, deadline - time.monotonic()))
00795             thread.join(wait)
00796         except BaseException as exc:                 # ANY failure of the join
00797             error = {'type': type(exc).__name__, 'detail': str(exc)}
00798         try:
00799             alive = bool(thread.is_alive())
00800             joined = not alive
00801         except BaseException as exc:                 # ANY failure of the query
00802             error = error or {'type': type(exc).__name__, 'detail': str(exc)}
00803             alive = None; joined = False
00804         facts.append({'name': name, 'start_state': state, 'started': True,
00805                       'alive': alive, 'joined': joined, 'error': error})
00806     return facts
00807 ```
00808 
00809 Properties:
00810 
00811 * **Every** owner is attempted — a failing `join` or a failing `is_alive` is
00812   recorded and the iteration continues.
00813 * The failure is **retained**, not swallowed: it is in the facts of the owner
00814   and it **fails the proof** (`_prove_salvage` must return a failure for an
00815   owner with `alive is None` or `error is not None`).
00816 * The cleanup is **bounded**: at most `seconds` (10 s) per owner and at most
00817   `total_seconds` (30 s) for the whole salvage; the wait of an owner is
00818   cropped by the remaining total.
00819 * The salvage is **separate** from the product: it renews no deadline of the
00820   round, it erases no retained resource and it never claims that the product
00821   released anything (the docstring of `T10:326-339` is kept).
00822 
00823 ### 4.6 C19 — the start state needs **proven provenance**
00824 
00825 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D5).** The classification rule itself stands;
00826 > a **failure** of the classification is now handled inside the per-owner
00827 > guard and is recorded with its diagnostic (§10.7).
00828 
00829 **Current (`T10:292-323`):** an owner without an identity that is not alive
00830 is mapped to `NEVER_STARTED` (`T10:323`) — a guess, not a proof.
00831 
00832 **Proposed (C19):**
00833 
00834 ```python
00835 def _owner_start_state(thread, hint=None):
00836     if thread is None:
00837         return 'NEVER_STARTED'
00838     ident = getattr(thread, 'ident', None)      # guarded by try/except
00839     if ident is not None:
00840         return 'STARTED'
00841     if hint in ('STARTED', 'NEVER_STARTED', 'UNKNOWN'):
00842         return hint                              # proven provenance (C17)
00843     return 'UNKNOWN'                             # no provenance => UNKNOWN
00844 ```
00845 
00846 `NEVER_STARTED` is now returned **only** when the registry proves that the
00847 start was never invoked (or when the thread object does not exist at all).
00848 An ident-less owner without provenance is `UNKNOWN` and **fails the proof**.
00849 
00850 ### 4.7 C20 — the stop: the exception **plus** the live state and the retention, before the salvage
00851 
00852 > **REVISED by §10 (root review D5, root factual correction).** The capture
00853 > names the **real** keys of the evidence DTO — including
00854 > `background_threads`, which is a valid key (`C:2399-2406`) — and keeps the
00855 > **object identities** (`session.broker is …`, `id(session.broker)`) apart
00856 > from the display JSON. A snapshot that fails records an explicit
00857 > `snapshot_error`; no key is invented and no valid key is read with a
00858 > `.get()` that could hide an absent value.
00859 
00860 **Current (`T10:396-412`):** on an exception the capture keeps only the type
00861 and the detail; the live state and the retained resources of the moment are
00862 lost.
00863 
00864 **Proposed (C20):**
00865 
00866 ```python
00867 def _capture_stop(session):
00868     captured = {'returned': None, 'exception': None, 'live_state': None,
00869                 'retained': None, 'retained_broker_id': None,
00870                 'background_threads': None}
00871     if session is None:
00872         return captured
00873     try:
00874         captured['returned'] = session.stop()
00875     except BaseException as error:
00876         captured['exception'] = {'type': type(error).__name__,
00877                                  'detail': str(error)}
00878         # the live state and the retention are read NOW, before the salvage
00879         try:
00880             captured['live_state'] = session.state
00881             captured['retained'] = session.broker is not None
00882             captured['retained_broker_id'] = id(session.broker)
00883             captured['background_threads'] = session.evidence().get(
00884                 'background_threads')
00885         except BaseException:                     # the facts stay visible
00886             captured['live_state'] = 'UNKNOWN'
00887     else:
00888         captured['retained'] = session.broker is not None
00889         captured['retained_broker_id'] = id(session.broker)
00890     return captured
00891 ```
00892 
00893 The stop exception is never discarded, and the live state / retention of the
00894 moment are recorded **before** the salvage of the fixture.
00895 
00896 ### 4.8 C21 — the reversed fallback arguments
00897 
00898 **Current (`T10:537-541`):**
00899 
00900 ```python
00901 if session is not None and 'session' not in kinds:
00902     add(_session_owners('%s:session' % prefix, session, hints))   # reversed
00903 if channel is not None and 'channel' not in kinds:
00904     add(_channel_owners('%s:channel' % prefix, channel, hints))   # reversed
00905 ```
00906 
00907 `_session_owners(session, prefix='session', hints=None)` and
00908 `_channel_owners(channel, prefix, hints)` take the **object first**; the
00909 fallback passes the **name string** as the object and the object as the
00910 prefix. The dedup key (`id(thread)`) is then computed over a string.
00911 
00912 **Proposed (C21):**
00913 
00914 ```python
00915 if session is not None and 'session' not in kinds:
00916     add(_session_owners(session, '%s:session' % prefix, hints))
00917 if channel is not None and 'channel' not in kinds:
00918     add(_channel_owners(channel, '%s:channel' % prefix, hints))
00919 ```
00920 
00921 (the registry-loop calls at `T10:529-534` are already in the correct order and
00922 are unchanged).
00923 
00924 ### 4.9 The deadline of the product is preserved
00925 
00926 Every wait of the fixture is the **fixture's** own bounded wait (≤ 10 s per
00927 owner, ≤ 30 s per salvage, ≤ 15 s per observation, ≤ 30 s per gate). None of
00928 them renews, extends or publishes a deadline of the round; the product's own
00929 cleanup deadline (`C:2121-2133`) and the original `STOP_CLEANUP_SECONDS`
00930 budget are untouched. The salvage is the work of the **test** and it is
00931 recorded separately from the returned state of the product.

01066 ## 10. Correction addendum — root review D1–D5 (authoritative)
01067 
01068 Revises the design after the root review (`CHANGES_REQUIRED`, D1–D5). It
01069 **supersedes** §3.5–§3.8, §4.2, §4.4–§4.7 and the rows C10, C11, C12, C14,
01070 C15, C17–C20, C22 of §6. Everything else stands (C1–C9, C13, C16, C21, §2,
01071 §5, §7–§9). No framework is added: the causal order, the exception boundaries,
01072 the inventory and the transitions of the named items are fixed.
01073 
01074 ### 10.1 (D1) — the barrier: the wait may not precede its cause
01075 
01076 **Withdrawn:** the `barrier_entered` event and the wait "right after
01077 `session.start()`" of §3.6 — the barrier of the seam runs only when the
01078 coordination cancels the read, which `bind_deadline` + `clock.advance`
01079 (`T10:4139-4140`) cause **after** the worker and the generation are
01080 registered (`T10:4125-4134`). The original trigger is preserved, never moved:
01081 
01082 | step | action | where |
01083 |---|---|---|
01084 | S1 | `session.start()` | `T10:4119` |
01085 | S2 | bounded wait 15 s for `api.read_waiting` | `T10:4123` |
01086 | S3 | `worker = holder['read_endpoint']._reader`; `api.worker_holder['worker'] = worker` | `T10:4125-4127` |
01087 | S4 | `generation = worker._submitted`; `api.worker_holder['generation'] = generation` | `T10:4128-4134` |
01088 | S5 | `bind_deadline(clock.value + 0.5)`; `clock.advance(1.0)` → the coordination cancels the read → the seam's `cancel_synchronous_io` runs | `T10:4139-4140` |
01089 | S6 | **in the seam**: publish the fault → the barrier block → the predicates → `barrier['left_at']` → **the seam persists `api.barrier_snapshot = dict(self.barrier)`** → **the seam sets `api.barrier_completed`** | seam `T10:3899-3994` |
01090 | S7 | the phase waits (bounded 15 s) for `api.barrier_completed` | new |
01091 | S8 | the phase writes the durable barrier document **from the persisted snapshot** | new |
01092 | S9 | the barrier assertions read the **persisted snapshot** | `T10:4192-4232` |
01093 
01094 * The event is **`barrier_completed`**, set by the seam at the **end** of the
01095   barrier block; no "entered" event, no wait before S5.
01096 * The snapshot is written **by the seam**; the phase never re-reads the live
01097   `api.barrier`, so a late snapshot can never look completed.
01098 * A **timeout** of S7 persists an explicit premise failure —
01099   `{'status': 'FAIL', 'premise': 'BARRIER_NOT_COMPLETED', 'timeout_seconds':
01100   15.0, 'barrier_completed': False}` — and the phase fails; it never
01101   continues with an empty barrier.
01102 * `expect_barrier='NOT_APPLICABLE'`: the barrier never runs, the document is
01103   written **immediately** with the empty snapshot and
01104   `barrier_snapshot['entered_at'] is None` is asserted (`T10:4227-4232`); no
01105   wait is performed there.
01106 * The failure path keeps the barrier facts (`T10:4304-4306`) and adds
01107   `barrier_completed` and the snapshot when it exists.
01108 
01109 ### 10.2 (D2) — the construction, the phase result, the whole-test guard
01110 
01111 **(a) The construction is inside the local guard**, with the holders
01112 initialised to `None` before it: `ledger.attempt(phase + '-construction')`,
01113 then `session = holder = channel_closes = channel_facts = None`, then `try:`
01114 → `_chain(api, document, plan, tmp_path, clock=clock)` → the phase body →
01115 `except BaseException:` (the FAIL rewrite of §10.6) → `raise` → `finally:`
01116 (the bounded teardown; a `None` holder is skipped, never dereferenced). A
01117 construction that failed half way is therefore an **attempted construction**
01118 with a durable FAIL document, not an absent document.
01119 
01120 **(b) The complete inventory** — five names per schedule: `<phase>` (the
01121 **result**), `<phase>-construction`, `<phase>-barrier`, `<phase>-first`,
01122 `<phase>-second`; plus `r10-published-before-timeout{,-first,-second}` and
01123 the earlier R10 documents `r10-first`, `r10-second`, `r10-coordination` →
01124 **31 names**, all `plan`ned at the top of the test.
01125 
01126 **(c) The result is separate from the checks.** A passed check is terminal.
01127 The result document is written **last**, after both stops **and** the cleanup,
01128 and becomes PASSED only when the barrier check is PASSED (or NOT_APPLICABLE),
01129 both stop checks are PASSED and the cleanup had no proof failure. A later
01130 failed stop ⇒ the result is **FAIL** while the earlier checks **keep** PASSED
01131 and their facts. The result is never PASSED before the stops and the cleanup.
01132 
01133 **(d) The whole-test guard** covers the earlier R10 real-chain work
01134 (`T10:4745-4816`), the coordination block (`T10:4817-4888`) **and** the five
01135 later schedules; the inventory and the ledger are installed before all of it;
01136 the `finally` writes `NOT_RUN` only for the names still PLANNED and never
01137 overwrites a written document.
01138 
01139 ### 10.3 (D3) — the scope, the exact thread objects, the bounded drain
01140 
01141 **(a) The scope** — one registry per round lifetime; the seam is armed for
01142 the whole lifetime and disarmed only after that round's salvage: the R07 main
01143 round (`parent_registry`, armed before `start_round(...)` at `T10:2371`,
01144 disarmed after the parent salvage at `T10:2983-2995`); the zero round
01145 (`zero_registry`, `T10:2682` → `T10:2786-2789`); each controlled subcase
01146 (`controlled_registry`, `T10:3221` → `T10:3370-3374`). The seam stays armed
01147 through the product's `stop()` and the late closer work, so a thread started
01148 during the stop is registered too.
01149 
01150 **(b) The exact object, not the name** — the registration is keyed by
01151 `id(thread)`; the name is only a label. The seam forwards every start it
01152 does not own (`if id(thread) not in armed_threads and thread.name not in
01153 owned_names: return original_start(thread, *args, **kwargs)`); the ownership
01154 proof always works on the object, and a name match alone never claims
01155 ownership.
01156 
01157 **(c) No production decision is frozen** — the seam observes only: it
01158 forwards the original start, never blocks, refuses, reorders or delays a
01159 start, and never touches a deadline.
01160 
01161 **(d) The bounded drain, ONE overall bound** — `pending_starts() == 0` alone
01162 is withdrawn as a proof (a start may follow the snapshot). The salvage of a
01163 round is a bounded drain loop: `budget = 30.0` (one overall bound per
01164 round), `deadline = now + budget`; then repeatedly — take `registry.snapshot()`
01165 (the exact objects and their states) and append it to `attempts`; release the
01166 gates of the round; `_salvage_threads(snapshot.owners, states=snapshot.hints,
01167 seconds=10.0, total_seconds=max(0.0, deadline - now))`; stop when
01168 `quiescent` (no pending start, no late start) **and** the salvage is proved,
01169 or when `now >= deadline`. The last snapshot and the last salvage are the
01170 recorded facts.
01171 
01172 * The **30 s** is the bound of the **whole drain of that round**, not 30 s per
01173   resnapshot; the per-owner wait is cropped by the remaining overall budget
01174   and the budget is **never reset** between the rounds of the loop nor between
01175   the rounds of the test.
01176 * The quiescence assertion comes **after** the drain, never before it: an
01177   unquiet round is a **FAIL/UNKNOWN** — the gates are still released and
01178   **all** the registered owners are still attempted; the drain repeats
01179   boundedly; if the bound is reached the proof fails truthfully (`'the owners
01180   of the round were not quiescent'`) with the last snapshot and the last
01181   salvage recorded.
01182 * The drain never renews a deadline of the product and never claims that the
01183   product released a resource.
01184 
01185 **(e) The producers** are the ones the product starts: pump and heartbeat
01186 (`C:1772-1783`), closer (`C:1530-1534`), channel drain (`B:5256-5278`), the
01187 two endpoint workers (`B:4683-4702`) — all observed, because the seam
01188 observes every `threading.Thread.start` of the armed window.
01189 
01190 ### 10.4 (D4) — the exact close failure, the exact unwinding order
01191 
01192 **(a) The substring test is withdrawn.** The oracle is exact: exactly one
01193 recorded failure; `owner == 'controlled:transport'`; `type == 'RuntimeError'`
01194 (the exact class); `detail == 'controlled_close_failure'` (the exact
01195 message); and no record with another owner or another type. In **every**
01196 checkpoint `child_close_failures` (`T10:2929-2964`) must be **empty**: an
01197 unrelated close or endpoint error fails the subcase instead of being
01198 tolerated next to the intended failure.
01199 
01200 **(b) The exact ordering** for the four checkpoints whose deliberate failure
01201 is raised by the fixture: (1) the deliberate failure is **raised** inside the
01202 region (sentinel / ordinary assertion / constructor seam); (2) the region
01203 runs **every** cleanup action in a fixed order — the gates → the close of the
01204 transport → the close of each endpoint → `_capture_stop` → the owner
01205 enumeration → the drain + salvage → the proof → the document; (3) the region
01206 **records** every additional error and raises `AssertionError(proof)` **only**
01207 when no original failure is unwinding; (4) the original failure leaves the
01208 region and is caught by the outer `except`, **after every other cleanup
01209 action has been attempted**; (5) the outer `except` records the exact type
01210 and the exact token.
01211 
01212 `CLOSE_FAILURE` is the single case whose failure is produced **by the
01213 cleanup itself**: the failing close is **recorded** with its exact type and
01214 exact message and the region **continues** with every other cleanup action —
01215 it is therefore **not** an unwinding case, and the design says so instead of
01216 claiming it. No expected sentinel is caught before the cleanup region: the
01217 outer `except` is the only catch and it lies outside the region.
01218 
01219 **(c) The original failure is preserved** — an error met by the region while
01220 an original failure unwinds leaves the **original** re-raised, the additional
01221 error recorded in the document and the overall proof failed; the test never
01222 reports a successful cleanup on an error.
01223 
01224 ### 10.5 (D5) — every cleanup error is preserved
01225 
01226 **(a) The classification is inside the per-owner guard** (it was outside the
01227 try of the salvage in §4.5). Per owner: `state = None; errors = []`; then
01228 `_owner_start_state(...)` inside its own `try` (a failure ⇒ an `errors`
01229 entry of kind `STATE` and `state = 'UNKNOWN'`); if the state is not
01230 `STARTED` the owner is recorded with `alive=None, joined=None` and its
01231 errors; otherwise `thread.join(wait)` in its own `try` (kind `JOIN`) and
01232 `bool(thread.is_alive())` in its own `try` (kind `LIVENESS`, `alive = None`
01233 on a failure); the fact of the owner keeps `alive`, `joined` and the **list**
01234 `errors`.
01235 
01236 * **every** owner is attempted — a failure of the classification, of the join
01237   or of the liveness query never aborts the iteration;
01238 * every error is retained in a **list** with its kind, exact type and detail
01239   — never a single "first error", never a silent `UNKNOWN` without a
01240   diagnostic; an owner whose classification failed is `UNKNOWN` **with** the
01241   diagnostic and it fails the proof, which names the owner and the error;
01242 * the display form (the thread name) and the identity (`id(thread)`) are
01243   separate fields — the identity is never read out of a display string.
01244 
01245 **(b) `KeyboardInterrupt` / `SystemExit`** — the interruption is recorded
01246 with its identity; with no original unwinding it is re-raised at the end of
01247 the region; with an original unwinding the **original** is preserved and
01248 re-raised and the interruption is an additional recorded error. The region
01249 never reports a successful cleanup when an interruption occurred.
01250 
01251 **(c) `_capture_stop` reads the real facts** — the **real** keys of the
01252 evidence DTO (`C:2343-2444`), among them `background_threads`, which **is** a
01253 valid key (`C:2399-2406`); the object identities are kept apart from the
01254 display JSON. The capture holds: `returned` (the actual dict of
01255 `session.stop()`), `exception` (`{'type','detail'}`), `live_state`
01256 (`session.state`), `evidence` (the full dict of `session.evidence()`),
01257 `evidence_state`, `evidence_broker_retained`, `evidence_failures`,
01258 `evidence_background_threads`, `evidence_closer_start_state` (the real keys
01259 of that dict), `retained_broker_is_session_broker` (a bool: the identity),
01260 `retained_broker_id` (`id(session.broker)`: the identity) and `snapshot_error`
01261 (`{'type','detail'}` when the snapshot failed).
01262 
01263 * the identities are **not** read out of the display JSON — they are the live
01264   facts of the session; the display JSON is kept as the DTO it is;
01265 * a valid key is never read through a `.get()` that could hide an absent
01266   value — a missing value is a fact to be asserted;
01267 * if the snapshot raises, `snapshot_error` carries the exact type and detail
01268   and the capture is **not** silently empty;
01269 * the capture is taken **before** the salvage and on **both** paths.
01270 
01271 ### 10.6 (D2, D6) — the state transitions after the corrections
01272 
01273 | from | event | to | durable document |
01274 |---|---|---|---|
01275 | `PLANNED` | the operation is entered (`attempt()` **before** the construction, the phase body, the barrier or the stop) | `ATTEMPTED` | none yet |
01276 | `PLANNED` | the end of the test, never entered | `NOT_RUN` | `{'status': 'NOT_RUN', 'reason': <type of the first failure>}` — no fact of the phase |
01277 | `ATTEMPTED` | the raw facts are written, before the assertions | `ATTEMPTED` | `{'status': 'EXECUTED', ...raw facts...}` |
01278 | `ATTEMPTED` | every check of the operation held | `PASSED` | the **check** document — terminal |
01279 | `ATTEMPTED` | an assertion raised or the operation itself raised | `FAIL` | the check document: `{'status': 'FAIL', 'executed': True, 'reason': <type>, 'detail': <str>, ...raw facts...}` |
01280 | `ATTEMPTED` | the phase reached its end | `PASSED` / `FAIL` | the **result** document, written **last**; PASSED only when the barrier check, both stop checks **and** the cleanup passed; a later failed stop ⇒ FAIL while the earlier checks keep PASSED |
01281 | `PASSED` / `FAIL` / `NOT_RUN` | anything | unchanged (**terminal**) | never overwritten by the inventory |
01282 
01283 The **result** and the **check** documents are different: the result carries
01284 the overall outcome, the checks carry their own facts; a failed check never
01285 rewrites a passed check and the inventory never rewrites either.
